He said: 'Be patient, O mother, for we are upon the truth.' Then she was thrown in with her child."

As for the companion of Jurayj:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zaʿfarani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil told us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib told us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿAbd Allah [ibn Hamid] [in the Isfahan manuscript: Dawud] informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Rashid ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah told us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man called Jurayj was a monk who worshipped in his hermitage. His mother came to greet him and called out: 'O Jurayj, come to me, let me see you.' He was praying and said: 'My mother and my prayer are for my Lord.' He preferred his prayer to his Lord over his mother. She went away, then she came a second time and called: 'O Jurayj, speak to me.' He was praying and chose his prayer. Then she came a third time and he chose his prayer. She said: 'He refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of the prostitutes of Madinah.' He said: 'If she had prayed against him to be tested, he would have been tested.'"

He said: there was a shepherd of sheep who used to stay near his monastery. A woman from the village came, and he had intercourse with her, and she conceived and gave birth to a boy. She was asked: "Whose is this?" She said: "From the owner of the hermitage." So they came to him, demolished his hermitage, and took him away to their king. When he passed by the shops of the prostitutes, they came out, and he smiled, realizing that it was the supplication of his mother. They said: "Why did he laugh when he passed the prostitutes?" When he was brought before their king, Jurayj said: "Where is the child you have borne?" The child was brought, and Jurayj said to him: "Who is your father?" He said: "My father is so-and-so the shepherd." Then Allah, exalted is He, cleared Jurayj, and the people honoured him. They said: "We will build your monastery for you with gold and silver." He said: "No, but restore it as it was," and he went up to it.

As for the child of the woman of the trench, we will mention it in its place, if Allah wills.

﴿He has given me the Book﴾, meaning "He will give me the Book." Its form is past but its meaning is future. It was also said: he was informing about what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, as when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "When were you written as a prophet?" He said: "I was written a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body."

[Musnad Ahmad: 5/59.]

It was also said: the meaning is that He taught me and inspired me with the Torah while I was in my mother's womb.

﴿And He has made me a prophet, and made me blessed, wherever I am﴾, a teacher of good. It was also said: blessed to whoever follows my religion and my command. ﴿And He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah as long as I live, and dutiful to my mother﴾, meaning He made me dutiful toward my mother, ﴿and He has not made me a tyrant, unblessed.﴾

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 19, verses 16–40 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) giving life to the dead and healing the blind and the leper, among the signs that Allah had permitted him to perform. She said: "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast that nursed you." Ibn Maryam replied to her: "Blessed is the one who recites the Book of Allah and follows what is in it, and is not a tyrant or a wretch." He would also say: "Ask me, for my heart is soft and I am small in my own eyes, owing to the humility that Allah, glorified is He, has granted me."

﴿Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ ﴿That is 'Isa son of Maryam, a statement of truth,﴾ meaning: it is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is in the nominative by repetition, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, and that is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is an epithet of 'Isa, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, the Word of Allah, and "the truth" is Allah, glorified is He.

ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read qawla in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: he said the statement of truth ﴿about which they dispute﴾, meaning: they doubt and say what is untrue. The Jews said: "A sorcerer, a liar," and the Christians said: "The son of Allah" and "the third of three." Then He refuted them, saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾, meaning: it is not of His attributes to take a son. It was also said: the lam is transposed, meaning: Allah would not take a son; ﴿glory be to Him!﴾ He declared Himself free of it. ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ That is what was in His knowledge. ﴿And indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is the straight path.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿Indeed Allah﴾ with a kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnaf). ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, meaning: the Christians. They were called factions because they split into three groups concerning the matter of 'Isa: the Nestorians, the Melkites, and the Jacobites (al-Mar Ya'qubiyya).

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿How much they will hear and see!﴾ meaning: how much they will hear and see, in an expression of wonder. That is because they will hear on the Day of Resurrection when hearing will not benefit them, and they will see when sight will not benefit them.

al-Kalbi said: No one on the Day of Resurrection will hear or see more than them, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to 'Isa: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾ and so on.

﴿The day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided﴾, meaning: when the reckoning is finished, the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, and death has been slaughtered, ﴿while they are heedless﴾ of the world.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan narrated to us, saying: [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq, from ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah, from] ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Saʿid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white-speckled ram. It will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' It will be commanded and slaughtered. Then a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! O people of the Fire, eternity without death!' So the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in sorrow upon their sorrow." [In the Isfahan manuscript: "It will be slaughtered, and it will be said."] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided, while they are in heedlessness﴾, and he pointed with his hand toward the world. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/9, with variation.]

Muqatil said: Were it not for what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, decreed concerning the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire and their remaining in it, they would die of regret when they saw that.

﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾, meaning: We cause them to die, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, remains, and He inherits them. ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾, so We will recompense them for their deeds.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 19, verses 16–40 (Part 1 of 2)**

﴿And mention in the Book, Maryam (Mary)﴾, the Qur'an. She was the daughter of ʿImran ibn Mathan, ﴿when she withdrew﴾.

Qatadah said: she isolated herself. al-Kalbi said: she moved aside. The root is *al-nabdhah* (with the *nun* either fathah or dammah), which means a side or a place apart. The meaning is that she withdrew and sat in an eastern place, ﴿a place facing east﴾, that is, a spot in the house on the side facing the east. She sat there because it was winter.

al-Hasan said: the Christians took the east as their qiblah because Maryam ﴿withdrew to a place facing east﴾.

﴿And she took a screen apart from them﴾, a veil.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: a curtain. Muqatil said: she placed a mountain between herself and her people. ʿIkrimah said: Maryam used to stay in the mosque as long as she was pure. When she menstruated, she moved to the house of her maternal aunt, and when she became pure again she returned to the mosque. While she was washing from her menstruation, Jibril appeared to her in the form of a beardless young man, of radiant face, curly-haired and well-formed.

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him). It was also said that the "Spirit" is the spirit of ʿIsa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), and the attribution to Him is one of specification and honour. ﴿And he presented himself to her as a well-formed human being﴾, ﴿tamaththal﴾ meaning he took the appearance of a human being to her, ﴿bashaaran sawiyyan﴾, a complete human, with nothing lacking. He sent him in the form of a human so that Maryam (peace be upon her) would be steadied and able to listen to his speech. Had he come to her in his true form, she would have been terrified, fled from him, and been unable to hear his words.

When Maryam saw him, she said: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾, meaning a believer and obedient.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: she knew that the *taqi* (God-fearing) is one who possesses restraint (*nahyah*).

It was also said: there was a God-fearing man, among the most just people of that time. Maryam said: "If you are as righteous as the God-fearing man, then ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you﴾." How could a man who is a stranger and a woman who is a stranger be under one veil? Jibril said to her: ﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you﴾. That is, he says "to give you" (*li-ahaba*). Abu ʿAmr read *li-yahaba* with the *ya'* (a third-person form, "that He may give"), ﴿a pure boy﴾, righteous and God-fearing.

Maryam said: ﴿How can I have a boy when no human has touched me﴾, meaning no human has approached me, ﴿and I have not been unchaste﴾, meaning not immoral. The *ha'* was dropped from *bagiyyan* (unchaste) because the word is turned away from its usual form.

Jibril said: ﴿So it will be﴾, as you said, O Maryam. But ﴿your Lord said﴾, and it was also said: ﴿Thus your Lord said﴾. ﴿It is easy for Me﴾, meaning creating a child without a father. ﴿And that We may make him a sign﴾, an indication, ﴿to the people, and a mercy from Us﴾ to whoever follows him in his religion.

﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾, something enumerated and written in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*).

﴿So she conceived him﴾. That was because Jibril (peace be upon him) lifted her garment and blew into her collar, so she conceived when she put it on. It was also said: Jibril blew from a distance, and the wind reached her and she conceived. When she had conceived, ﴿she withdrew﴾, went out and isolated herself, ﴿to a remote place﴾, far from her family, beyond the mountain. It is said: at the far end of the house.

al-Kalbi said: it was said to a paternal cousin of hers named Yusuf: "Maryam has conceived from fornication," so that the king would kill her, for she had already been reported to him. He came to her and took her away, and fled with her. When they were on part of the road, Yusuf, her cousin, wanted to kill her. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "She is from the Holy Spirit, so do not kill her." So he left her, did not kill her, and remained with her.

They differed about the length of her pregnancy and the time of her delivery. Some said her pregnancy lasted nine months, like that of other women. Others said eight months, and that this was another sign, because no child born after eight months survived except ʿIsa. It was also said six months, and it was said three hours, and it was said one hour.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was only that she conceived and gave birth, and there was no interval between the conception and her withdrawal except one hour, because Allah, exalted is He, did not mention any separation between them.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: Maryam conceived him in an hour, he was formed in an hour, and she delivered him in an hour, when the sun had passed its zenith on that day. She was ten years old, and she had menstruated twice before she conceived ʿIsa.

﴿Then the pains of labour drove her﴾, meaning they forced her and brought her, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud): *awaha* (sheltered). That means the pregnancy, and it was also said: the labour pains.

﴿To the trunk of the palm tree﴾. It was a dry palm in the desert in the depth of winter, with no fronds.

Hilal ibn Khabbab narrated from Abu ʿUbaydullah: it was a dry trunk that had been brought to build with, a place called the House of Lahm (Bethlehem).

﴿She said: "Would that I had died before this, and had become a thing forgotten."﴾ Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read *nasyan* with a fathah on the *nun*, and the others read it with a kasrah. Both are dialect forms, like *al-watr* and *al-witr*, *al-hajr* and *al-hijr*, *al-jisr* and *al-jasr*, and it means a thing forgotten.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: meaning a thing abandoned. Qatadah said: a thing that is not remembered or known. ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: a discarded menstrual rag. al-Rabiʿ said: a miscarriage. Muqatil said: meaning like a destroyed thing. ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Muslim said: meaning one who was not created. al-Farraʾ said: it is what a woman throws away of the cloths used during her menstruation. Abu ʿUbayd said: it is what is forgotten and neglected of a trivial thing. al-Kumayt said:

*"Will you make us a bridge for the Kalb of Qudaʿah,*
*while we are not forgotten among Maʿadd nor an insignificant tribe?"*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/93.]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: "I wish that when I die I were a thing forgotten."

﴿Then he called her from beneath her﴾. al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *min tahtiha* with a kasrah on the *mim*, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him), who called to her from the foot of the mountain. The others read *man tahtaha* with a fathah on the *mim*, meaning ʿIsa, who, when he came out of her womb, called to her: ﴿Do not grieve, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾.

al-Hasan said: meaning ʿIsa. By Allah, he was a servant (*sariyy*), that is, noble. The other exegetes said it is a small stream. It was also said that the meaning of His words *tahtaki* (beneath you) is that Allah, exalted is He, placed the stream under her command: if she ordered it to flow, it flowed, and if she ordered it to stop, it stopped. This is like His words, related about Pharaoh: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾, meaning under my command. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Jibril struck the ground with his foot, or it is said ʿIsa struck the ground with his foot, and a spring of sweet water appeared and flowed. The palm tree, which had dried up, came back to life, put forth leaves, bore fruit, and produced ripe dates.

It was said to Maryam: ﴿And shake towards you﴾, that is, move, ﴿the trunk of the palm tree﴾. The Arabs say *hazzahu* and *hazza bihi*, as they say *khudh al-khitam* and *khudh bi-l-khitam* (take the halter), *ta'allaqa bi-Zayd* and *ta'allaqa Zaydan* (he clung to Zayd), *khudh ra'sahu* and *khudh bi-ra'sihi*, and *imdud al-habl* and *imdud bi-l-habl* (stretch the rope). The *jidhʿ* means a branch, and the *jidhʿ* also means the palm tree itself.

﴿It will drop upon you﴾. al-Bara ibn ʿAzib, Yaʿqub, Abu Hatim, Hammad and Nasir read *yusaqit* with a *ya'*. Hafs read *tusaqit* with a dammah on the *ta'*, a sukun on the *sin* and a kasrah on the *qaf*. al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and Abu ʿUbayd read *tassaqat* with a fathah on the *ta'* and the *qaf*, and a shaddah on the *sin*. Whoever read it feminine referred it to the palm, and whoever read it masculine referred it to the trunk. The shaddah indicates assimilation (*idghaam*), and the lightened form indicates deletion (*hadhf*).

﴿Ripe dates, fresh﴾, meaning a branch of moist dates, fresh at the time of picking.

al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym said: for a woman who has just given birth there is nothing better in my view than dates, and nothing better for a sick person than honey.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: I do not know of anything better for a woman whose child is difficult to deliver than dates, because of the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Shake towards you the trunk of the palm, it will drop upon you ripe dates, fresh﴾.

ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: it is among the Sunnah to chew dates and rub them on the mouth of a newborn. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to chew dates and rub them on the palate of the children of the Companions.

﴿So eat, O Maryam, and drink, and be comforted﴾, that is, let your eye be cool and your soul be at rest. ﴿And if you see any human, say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾, that is, silence. This is why it was read in the recitation of Ibn Masʿud and Anas as *sawm* (fast). In the language, *sawm* means abstaining from food and speech. There is an abridgement in the verse: ﴿If you see any human﴾ and he asks you about your child or blames you for it, ﴿then say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾. It is said that Allah commanded her to say this as a sign. It is also said that she was commanded to say it aloud, and then to remain silent after that.

﴿So I will not speak today to any human﴾. It is said: she used to speak with the angels and not speak with humans.

﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾. al-Kalbi said: Yusuf the carpenter took Maryam and her son ʿIsa (peace be upon him) to a cave and placed them in it for forty days until she was purified of her postnatal bleeding. Then he brought her out. ﴿She brought him﴾ means she brought ʿIsa, ﴿carrying him﴾, after forty days. ʿIsa spoke to her on the road and said: "O mother, be glad, for I am the servant of Allah and His Messiah." When she entered upon her family with the child, they wept and grieved, for they were a righteous household.

They said: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with a thing monstrous﴾, that is, grave, outrageous and enormous. Abu ʿUbaydah said: everything that is astonishing or is done is *fari*. The Prophet (ﷺ) said of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "I have not seen a *ʿabqari* who does his *fariyy*," meaning one who does his deed.

[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 12/232; Zad al-Masir: 5/159; Musnad Ahmad: 2/28, with variation.]

The rajaz poet said:

*"You have fed me sour old dates, one year old,*
*wormy, stiff, and hard,*
*and you have indeed been loud in praising them."*

Meaning: you have increased your speech about them and magnified them.

﴿O sister of Harun﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They meant Harun the Prophet, the brother of Musa, because she was of his lineage."

Qatadah and others said: Harun was a righteous man among the God-fearing of the Children of Israel, and he was not Harun the brother of Musa. It was reported to us that forty thousand people, all named Harun from the Children of Israel, followed his funeral when he died.

al-Mughirah ibn Shuʿbah said: the people of Najran said to me: "His words, ʿO sister of Harun,' and between Musa and ʿIsa there were what years there were." I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and the righteous who came before them?"

al-Kalbi said: Harun was the brother of Maryam from her father, not from her mother, and he was the most excellent man among the Children of Israel. It was also said: Harun was among the most immoral and most openly corrupt of the Children of Israel, so they likened her to him. According to this view, *ukht* (sister) here means likeness, not kinship, and the Arabs call the likeness of a thing its sister or brother. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning its likeness.

﴿Your father ʿImran was not a man of evil, nor was your mother Hannah unchaste﴾, meaning an adulteress. So from where did you get this child?

Then Maryam pointed to ʿIsa, telling them to speak to him. ﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾, that is, one who is in the cradle, meaning in her lap. It was also said: it is the cradle itself. The word was filler in speech and has no independent meaning, as in His words: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, meaning you are the best nation. Likewise His words: ﴿Was I not but a human messenger?﴾, meaning "Am I not?" And as people say: "If you are my friend, then join me." Zuhayr said:

*"She was ridden upon by a noble Arab mare,*
*when the night's colour was like the darkest black."*

Al-Farazdaq said:

*"How will it be when you see the abodes of my people,*
*and our noble neighbours?"*

Meaning: and our noble neighbours.

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/100; al-Tibyan: 7/123.]

Wahb said: Zakariyya came to her when she was debating the Jews, and said to ʿIsa: "Speak your proof, if you have been commanded to do so." Then ʿIsa said, at the age of forty days. Muqatil said: it was on the day he was born.

﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah."﴾ He acknowledged his servanthood to Allah, exalted is He, as the first thing he said, as a refutation of the Christians and as establishing the proof against them.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: when Maryam brought ʿIsa to her people, they picked up stones to stone her. When ʿIsa spoke, they left her. They said: then ʿIsa did not speak again after this until he became like other children.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Five spoke before the age of speech: the witness of Yusuf, the child of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, ʿIsa, the companion of Jurayj, and the child of the woman who was burned in the trench."

As for the witness of Yusuf, his mention has already passed. As for the child of the hairdresser:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance passed by him. He said: "O Jibril, what is this fragrance?" He said: "It is the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter. She was combing her hair when the comb fell from her hand, and she said: 'In the name of Allah.' Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'My father?' She said: 'No, but my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of your father.' She said: 'I will tell my father about that.' She said: 'Yes.' So she told him, and he summoned her and said: 'Who is your Lord?' She said: 'My Lord and your Lord is in heaven.' So Pharaoh ordered a cow of brass to be heated. He summoned her and her children and she said: 'I have a request of you.' He said: 'What is it?' She said: 'Gather my bones and the bones of my children and bury them together.' He said: 'That is due to you from us as a right.' So he ordered her children to be thrown in one by one, until the last of her children, who was a nursing infant. He said: 'Be patient, O mother, for we are upon the truth.' Then she was thrown in with her child."

As for the companion of Jurayj:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zaʿfarani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil told us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib told us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿAbd Allah [ibn Hamid] [in the Isfahan manuscript: Dawud] informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Rashid ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah told us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man called Jurayj was a monk who worshipped in his hermitage. His mother came to greet him and called out: 'O Jurayj, come to me, let me see you.' He was praying and said: 'My mother and my prayer are for my Lord.' He preferred his prayer to his Lord over his mother. She went away, then she came a second time and called: 'O Jurayj, speak to me.' He was praying and chose his prayer. Then she came a third time and he chose his prayer. She said: 'He refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of the prostitutes of Madinah.' He said: 'If she had prayed against him to be tested, he would have been tested.'"

He said: there was a shepherd of sheep who used to stay near his monastery. A woman from the village came, and he had intercourse with her, and she conceived and gave birth to a boy. She was asked: "Whose is this?" She said: "From the owner of the hermitage." So they came to him, demolished his hermitage, and took him away to their king. When he passed by the shops of the prostitutes, they came out, and he smiled, realizing that it was the supplication of his mother. They said: "Why did he laugh when he passed the prostitutes?" When he was brought before their king, Jurayj said: "Where is the child you have borne?" The child was brought, and Jurayj said to him: "Who is your father?" He said: "My father is so-and-so the shepherd." Then Allah, exalted is He, cleared Jurayj, and the people honoured him. They said: "We will build your monastery for you with gold and silver." He said: "No, but restore it as it was," and he went up to it.

As for the child of the woman of the trench, we will mention it in its place, if Allah wills.

﴿He has given me the Book﴾, meaning "He will give me the Book." Its form is past but its meaning is future. It was also said: he was informing about what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, as when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "When were you written as a prophet?" He said: "I was written a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body."

[Musnad Ahmad: 5/59.]

It was also said: the meaning is that He taught me and inspired me with the Torah while I was in my mother's womb.

﴿And He has made me a prophet, and made me blessed, wherever I am﴾, a teacher of good. It was also said: blessed to whoever follows my religion and my command. ﴿And He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah as long as I live, and dutiful to my mother﴾, meaning He made me dutiful toward my mother, ﴿and He has not made me a tyrant, unblessed.﴾

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 19, verses 16–40 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) giving life to the dead and healing the blind and the leper, among the signs that Allah had permitted him to perform. She said: "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast that nursed you." Ibn Maryam replied to her: "Blessed is the one who recites the Book of Allah and follows what is in it, and is not a tyrant or a wretch." He would also say: "Ask me, for my heart is soft and I am small in my own eyes, owing to the humility that Allah, glorified is He, has granted me."

﴿Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ ﴿That is 'Isa son of Maryam, a statement of truth,﴾ meaning: it is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is in the nominative by repetition, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, and that is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is an epithet of 'Isa, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, the Word of Allah, and "the truth" is Allah, glorified is He.

ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read qawla in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: he said the statement of truth ﴿about which they dispute﴾, meaning: they doubt and say what is untrue. The Jews said: "A sorcerer, a liar," and the Christians said: "The son of Allah" and "the third of three." Then He refuted them, saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾, meaning: it is not of His attributes to take a son. It was also said: the lam is transposed, meaning: Allah would not take a son; ﴿glory be to Him!﴾ He declared Himself free of it. ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ That is what was in His knowledge. ﴿And indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is the straight path.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿Indeed Allah﴾ with a kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnaf). ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, meaning: the Christians. They were called factions because they split into three groups concerning the matter of 'Isa: the Nestorians, the Melkites, and the Jacobites (al-Mar Ya'qubiyya).

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿How much they will hear and see!﴾ meaning: how much they will hear and see, in an expression of wonder. That is because they will hear on the Day of Resurrection when hearing will not benefit them, and they will see when sight will not benefit them.

al-Kalbi said: No one on the Day of Resurrection will hear or see more than them, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to 'Isa: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾ and so on.

﴿The day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided﴾, meaning: when the reckoning is finished, the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, and death has been slaughtered, ﴿while they are heedless﴾ of the world.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan narrated to us, saying: [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq, from ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah, from] ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Saʿid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white-speckled ram. It will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' It will be commanded and slaughtered. Then a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! O people of the Fire, eternity without death!' So the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in sorrow upon their sorrow." [In the Isfahan manuscript: "It will be slaughtered, and it will be said."] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided, while they are in heedlessness﴾, and he pointed with his hand toward the world. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/9, with variation.]

Muqatil said: Were it not for what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, decreed concerning the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire and their remaining in it, they would die of regret when they saw that.

﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾, meaning: We cause them to die, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, remains, and He inherits them. ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾, so We will recompense them for their deeds.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 19, verses 16–40 (Part 1 of 2)**

﴿And mention in the Book, Maryam (Mary)﴾, the Qur'an. She was the daughter of ʿImran ibn Mathan, ﴿when she withdrew﴾.

Qatadah said: she isolated herself. al-Kalbi said: she moved aside. The root is *al-nabdhah* (with the *nun* either fathah or dammah), which means a side or a place apart. The meaning is that she withdrew and sat in an eastern place, ﴿a place facing east﴾, that is, a spot in the house on the side facing the east. She sat there because it was winter.

al-Hasan said: the Christians took the east as their qiblah because Maryam ﴿withdrew to a place facing east﴾.

﴿And she took a screen apart from them﴾, a veil.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: a curtain. Muqatil said: she placed a mountain between herself and her people. ʿIkrimah said: Maryam used to stay in the mosque as long as she was pure. When she menstruated, she moved to the house of her maternal aunt, and when she became pure again she returned to the mosque. While she was washing from her menstruation, Jibril appeared to her in the form of a beardless young man, of radiant face, curly-haired and well-formed.

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him). It was also said that the "Spirit" is the spirit of ʿIsa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), and the attribution to Him is one of specification and honour. ﴿And he presented himself to her as a well-formed human being﴾, ﴿tamaththal﴾ meaning he took the appearance of a human being to her, ﴿bashaaran sawiyyan﴾, a complete human, with nothing lacking. He sent him in the form of a human so that Maryam (peace be upon her) would be steadied and able to listen to his speech. Had he come to her in his true form, she would have been terrified, fled from him, and been unable to hear his words.

When Maryam saw him, she said: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾, meaning a believer and obedient.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: she knew that the *taqi* (God-fearing) is one who possesses restraint (*nahyah*).

It was also said: there was a God-fearing man, among the most just people of that time. Maryam said: "If you are as righteous as the God-fearing man, then ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you﴾." How could a man who is a stranger and a woman who is a stranger be under one veil? Jibril said to her: ﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you﴾. That is, he says "to give you" (*li-ahaba*). Abu ʿAmr read *li-yahaba* with the *ya'* (a third-person form, "that He may give"), ﴿a pure boy﴾, righteous and God-fearing.

Maryam said: ﴿How can I have a boy when no human has touched me﴾, meaning no human has approached me, ﴿and I have not been unchaste﴾, meaning not immoral. The *ha'* was dropped from *bagiyyan* (unchaste) because the word is turned away from its usual form.

Jibril said: ﴿So it will be﴾, as you said, O Maryam. But ﴿your Lord said﴾, and it was also said: ﴿Thus your Lord said﴾. ﴿It is easy for Me﴾, meaning creating a child without a father. ﴿And that We may make him a sign﴾, an indication, ﴿to the people, and a mercy from Us﴾ to whoever follows him in his religion.

﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾, something enumerated and written in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*).

﴿So she conceived him﴾. That was because Jibril (peace be upon him) lifted her garment and blew into her collar, so she conceived when she put it on. It was also said: Jibril blew from a distance, and the wind reached her and she conceived. When she had conceived, ﴿she withdrew﴾, went out and isolated herself, ﴿to a remote place﴾, far from her family, beyond the mountain. It is said: at the far end of the house.

al-Kalbi said: it was said to a paternal cousin of hers named Yusuf: "Maryam has conceived from fornication," so that the king would kill her, for she had already been reported to him. He came to her and took her away, and fled with her. When they were on part of the road, Yusuf, her cousin, wanted to kill her. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "She is from the Holy Spirit, so do not kill her." So he left her, did not kill her, and remained with her.

They differed about the length of her pregnancy and the time of her delivery. Some said her pregnancy lasted nine months, like that of other women. Others said eight months, and that this was another sign, because no child born after eight months survived except ʿIsa. It was also said six months, and it was said three hours, and it was said one hour.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was only that she conceived and gave birth, and there was no interval between the conception and her withdrawal except one hour, because Allah, exalted is He, did not mention any separation between them.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: Maryam conceived him in an hour, he was formed in an hour, and she delivered him in an hour, when the sun had passed its zenith on that day. She was ten years old, and she had menstruated twice before she conceived ʿIsa.

﴿Then the pains of labour drove her﴾, meaning they forced her and brought her, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud): *awaha* (sheltered). That means the pregnancy, and it was also said: the labour pains.

﴿To the trunk of the palm tree﴾. It was a dry palm in the desert in the depth of winter, with no fronds.

Hilal ibn Khabbab narrated from Abu ʿUbaydullah: it was a dry trunk that had been brought to build with, a place called the House of Lahm (Bethlehem).

﴿She said: "Would that I had died before this, and had become a thing forgotten."﴾ Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read *nasyan* with a fathah on the *nun*, and the others read it with a kasrah. Both are dialect forms, like *al-watr* and *al-witr*, *al-hajr* and *al-hijr*, *al-jisr* and *al-jasr*, and it means a thing forgotten.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: meaning a thing abandoned. Qatadah said: a thing that is not remembered or known. ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: a discarded menstrual rag. al-Rabiʿ said: a miscarriage. Muqatil said: meaning like a destroyed thing. ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Muslim said: meaning one who was not created. al-Farraʾ said: it is what a woman throws away of the cloths used during her menstruation. Abu ʿUbayd said: it is what is forgotten and neglected of a trivial thing. al-Kumayt said:

*"Will you make us a bridge for the Kalb of Qudaʿah,*
*while we are not forgotten among Maʿadd nor an insignificant tribe?"*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/93.]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: "I wish that when I die I were a thing forgotten."

﴿Then he called her from beneath her﴾. al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *min tahtiha* with a kasrah on the *mim*, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him), who called to her from the foot of the mountain. The others read *man tahtaha* with a fathah on the *mim*, meaning ʿIsa, who, when he came out of her womb, called to her: ﴿Do not grieve, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾.

al-Hasan said: meaning ʿIsa. By Allah, he was a servant (*sariyy*), that is, noble. The other exegetes said it is a small stream. It was also said that the meaning of His words *tahtaki* (beneath you) is that Allah, exalted is He, placed the stream under her command: if she ordered it to flow, it flowed, and if she ordered it to stop, it stopped. This is like His words, related about Pharaoh: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾, meaning under my command. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Jibril struck the ground with his foot, or it is said ʿIsa struck the ground with his foot, and a spring of sweet water appeared and flowed. The palm tree, which had dried up, came back to life, put forth leaves, bore fruit, and produced ripe dates.

It was said to Maryam: ﴿And shake towards you﴾, that is, move, ﴿the trunk of the palm tree﴾. The Arabs say *hazzahu* and *hazza bihi*, as they say *khudh al-khitam* and *khudh bi-l-khitam* (take the halter), *ta'allaqa bi-Zayd* and *ta'allaqa Zaydan* (he clung to Zayd), *khudh ra'sahu* and *khudh bi-ra'sihi*, and *imdud al-habl* and *imdud bi-l-habl* (stretch the rope). The *jidhʿ* means a branch, and the *jidhʿ* also means the palm tree itself.

﴿It will drop upon you﴾. al-Bara ibn ʿAzib, Yaʿqub, Abu Hatim, Hammad and Nasir read *yusaqit* with a *ya'*. Hafs read *tusaqit* with a dammah on the *ta'*, a sukun on the *sin* and a kasrah on the *qaf*. al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and Abu ʿUbayd read *tassaqat* with a fathah on the *ta'* and the *qaf*, and a shaddah on the *sin*. Whoever read it feminine referred it to the palm, and whoever read it masculine referred it to the trunk. The shaddah indicates assimilation (*idghaam*), and the lightened form indicates deletion (*hadhf*).

﴿Ripe dates, fresh﴾, meaning a branch of moist dates, fresh at the time of picking.

al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym said: for a woman who has just given birth there is nothing better in my view than dates, and nothing better for a sick person than honey.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: I do not know of anything better for a woman whose child is difficult to deliver than dates, because of the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Shake towards you the trunk of the palm, it will drop upon you ripe dates, fresh﴾.

ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: it is among the Sunnah to chew dates and rub them on the mouth of a newborn. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to chew dates and rub them on the palate of the children of the Companions.

﴿So eat, O Maryam, and drink, and be comforted﴾, that is, let your eye be cool and your soul be at rest. ﴿And if you see any human, say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾, that is, silence. This is why it was read in the recitation of Ibn Masʿud and Anas as *sawm* (fast). In the language, *sawm* means abstaining from food and speech. There is an abridgement in the verse: ﴿If you see any human﴾ and he asks you about your child or blames you for it, ﴿then say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾. It is said that Allah commanded her to say this as a sign. It is also said that she was commanded to say it aloud, and then to remain silent after that.

﴿So I will not speak today to any human﴾. It is said: she used to speak with the angels and not speak with humans.

﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾. al-Kalbi said: Yusuf the carpenter took Maryam and her son ʿIsa (peace be upon him) to a cave and placed them in it for forty days until she was purified of her postnatal bleeding. Then he brought her out. ﴿She brought him﴾ means she brought ʿIsa, ﴿carrying him﴾, after forty days. ʿIsa spoke to her on the road and said: "O mother, be glad, for I am the servant of Allah and His Messiah." When she entered upon her family with the child, they wept and grieved, for they were a righteous household.

They said: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with a thing monstrous﴾, that is, grave, outrageous and enormous. Abu ʿUbaydah said: everything that is astonishing or is done is *fari*. The Prophet (ﷺ) said of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "I have not seen a *ʿabqari* who does his *fariyy*," meaning one who does his deed.

[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 12/232; Zad al-Masir: 5/159; Musnad Ahmad: 2/28, with variation.]

The rajaz poet said:

*"You have fed me sour old dates, one year old,*
*wormy, stiff, and hard,*
*and you have indeed been loud in praising them."*

Meaning: you have increased your speech about them and magnified them.

﴿O sister of Harun﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They meant Harun the Prophet, the brother of Musa, because she was of his lineage."

Qatadah and others said: Harun was a righteous man among the God-fearing of the Children of Israel, and he was not Harun the brother of Musa. It was reported to us that forty thousand people, all named Harun from the Children of Israel, followed his funeral when he died.

al-Mughirah ibn Shuʿbah said: the people of Najran said to me: "His words, ʿO sister of Harun,' and between Musa and ʿIsa there were what years there were." I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and the righteous who came before them?"

al-Kalbi said: Harun was the brother of Maryam from her father, not from her mother, and he was the most excellent man among the Children of Israel. It was also said: Harun was among the most immoral and most openly corrupt of the Children of Israel, so they likened her to him. According to this view, *ukht* (sister) here means likeness, not kinship, and the Arabs call the likeness of a thing its sister or brother. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning its likeness.

﴿Your father ʿImran was not a man of evil, nor was your mother Hannah unchaste﴾, meaning an adulteress. So from where did you get this child?

Then Maryam pointed to ʿIsa, telling them to speak to him. ﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾, that is, one who is in the cradle, meaning in her lap. It was also said: it is the cradle itself. The word was filler in speech and has no independent meaning, as in His words: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, meaning you are the best nation. Likewise His words: ﴿Was I not but a human messenger?﴾, meaning "Am I not?" And as people say: "If you are my friend, then join me." Zuhayr said:

*"She was ridden upon by a noble Arab mare,*
*when the night's colour was like the darkest black."*

Al-Farazdaq said:

*"How will it be when you see the abodes of my people,*
*and our noble neighbours?"*

Meaning: and our noble neighbours.

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/100; al-Tibyan: 7/123.]

Wahb said: Zakariyya came to her when she was debating the Jews, and said to ʿIsa: "Speak your proof, if you have been commanded to do so." Then ʿIsa said, at the age of forty days. Muqatil said: it was on the day he was born.

﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah."﴾ He acknowledged his servanthood to Allah, exalted is He, as the first thing he said, as a refutation of the Christians and as establishing the proof against them.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: when Maryam brought ʿIsa to her people, they picked up stones to stone her. When ʿIsa spoke, they left her. They said: then ʿIsa did not speak again after this until he became like other children.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Five spoke before the age of speech: the witness of Yusuf, the child of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, ʿIsa, the companion of Jurayj, and the child of the woman who was burned in the trench."

As for the witness of Yusuf, his mention has already passed. As for the child of the hairdresser:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance passed by him. He said: "O Jibril, what is this fragrance?" He said: "It is the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter. She was combing her hair when the comb fell from her hand, and she said: 'In the name of Allah.' Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'My father?' She said: 'No, but my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of your father.' She said: 'I will tell my father about that.' She said: 'Yes.' So she told him, and he summoned her and said: 'Who is your Lord?' She said: 'My Lord and your Lord is in heaven.' So Pharaoh ordered a cow of brass to be heated. He summoned her and her children and she said: 'I have a request of you.' He said: 'What is it?' She said: 'Gather my bones and the bones of my children and bury them together.' He said: 'That is due to you from us as a right.' So he ordered her children to be thrown in one by one, until the last of her children, who was a nursing infant. He said: 'Be patient, O mother, for we are upon the truth.' Then she was thrown in with her child."

As for the companion of Jurayj:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zaʿfarani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil told us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib told us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿAbd Allah [ibn Hamid] [in the Isfahan manuscript: Dawud] informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Rashid ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah told us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man called Jurayj was a monk who worshipped in his hermitage. His mother came to greet him and called out: 'O Jurayj, come to me, let me see you.' He was praying and said: 'My mother and my prayer are for my Lord.' He preferred his prayer to his Lord over his mother. She went away, then she came a second time and called: 'O Jurayj, speak to me.' He was praying and chose his prayer. Then she came a third time and he chose his prayer. She said: 'He refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of the prostitutes of Madinah.' He said: 'If she had prayed against him to be tested, he would have been tested.'"

He said: there was a shepherd of sheep who used to stay near his monastery. A woman from the village came, and he had intercourse with her, and she conceived and gave birth to a boy. She was asked: "Whose is this?" She said: "From the owner of the hermitage." So they came to him, demolished his hermitage, and took him away to their king. When he passed by the shops of the prostitutes, they came out, and he smiled, realizing that it was the supplication of his mother. They said: "Why did he laugh when he passed the prostitutes?" When he was brought before their king, Jurayj said: "Where is the child you have borne?" The child was brought, and Jurayj said to him: "Who is your father?" He said: "My father is so-and-so the shepherd." Then Allah, exalted is He, cleared Jurayj, and the people honoured him. They said: "We will build your monastery for you with gold and silver." He said: "No, but restore it as it was," and he went up to it.

As for the child of the woman of the trench, we will mention it in its place, if Allah wills.

﴿He has given me the Book﴾, meaning "He will give me the Book." Its form is past but its meaning is future. It was also said: he was informing about what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, as when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "When were you written as a prophet?" He said: "I was written a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body."

[Musnad Ahmad: 5/59.]

It was also said: the meaning is that He taught me and inspired me with the Torah while I was in my mother's womb.

﴿And He has made me a prophet, and made me blessed, wherever I am﴾, a teacher of good. It was also said: blessed to whoever follows my religion and my command. ﴿And He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah as long as I live, and dutiful to my mother﴾, meaning He made me dutiful toward my mother, ﴿and He has not made me a tyrant, unblessed.﴾

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 19, verses 16–40 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) giving life to the dead and healing the blind and the leper, among the signs that Allah had permitted him to perform. She said: "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast that nursed you." Ibn Maryam replied to her: "Blessed is the one who recites the Book of Allah and follows what is in it, and is not a tyrant or a wretch." He would also say: "Ask me, for my heart is soft and I am small in my own eyes, owing to the humility that Allah, glorified is He, has granted me."

﴿Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ ﴿That is 'Isa son of Maryam, a statement of truth,﴾ meaning: it is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is in the nominative by repetition, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, and that is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is an epithet of 'Isa, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, the Word of Allah, and "the truth" is Allah, glorified is He.

ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read qawla in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: he said the statement of truth ﴿about which they dispute﴾, meaning: they doubt and say what is untrue. The Jews said: "A sorcerer, a liar," and the Christians said: "The son of Allah" and "the third of three." Then He refuted them, saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾, meaning: it is not of His attributes to take a son. It was also said: the lam is transposed, meaning: Allah would not take a son; ﴿glory be to Him!﴾ He declared Himself free of it. ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ That is what was in His knowledge. ﴿And indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is the straight path.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿Indeed Allah﴾ with a kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnaf). ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, meaning: the Christians. They were called factions because they split into three groups concerning the matter of 'Isa: the Nestorians, the Melkites, and the Jacobites (al-Mar Ya'qubiyya).

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿How much they will hear and see!﴾ meaning: how much they will hear and see, in an expression of wonder. That is because they will hear on the Day of Resurrection when hearing will not benefit them, and they will see when sight will not benefit them.

al-Kalbi said: No one on the Day of Resurrection will hear or see more than them, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to 'Isa: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾ and so on.

﴿The day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided﴾, meaning: when the reckoning is finished, the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, and death has been slaughtered, ﴿while they are heedless﴾ of the world.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan narrated to us, saying: [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq, from ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah, from] ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Saʿid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white-speckled ram. It will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' It will be commanded and slaughtered. Then a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! O people of the Fire, eternity without death!' So the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in sorrow upon their sorrow." [In the Isfahan manuscript: "It will be slaughtered, and it will be said."] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided, while they are in heedlessness﴾, and he pointed with his hand toward the world. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/9, with variation.]

Muqatil said: Were it not for what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, decreed concerning the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire and their remaining in it, they would die of regret when they saw that.

﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾, meaning: We cause them to die, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, remains, and He inherits them. ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾, so We will recompense them for their deeds.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 19, verses 16–40 (Part 1 of 2)**

﴿And mention in the Book, Maryam (Mary)﴾, the Qur'an. She was the daughter of ʿImran ibn Mathan, ﴿when she withdrew﴾.

Qatadah said: she isolated herself. al-Kalbi said: she moved aside. The root is *al-nabdhah* (with the *nun* either fathah or dammah), which means a side or a place apart. The meaning is that she withdrew and sat in an eastern place, ﴿a place facing east﴾, that is, a spot in the house on the side facing the east. She sat there because it was winter.

al-Hasan said: the Christians took the east as their qiblah because Maryam ﴿withdrew to a place facing east﴾.

﴿And she took a screen apart from them﴾, a veil.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: a curtain. Muqatil said: she placed a mountain between herself and her people. ʿIkrimah said: Maryam used to stay in the mosque as long as she was pure. When she menstruated, she moved to the house of her maternal aunt, and when she became pure again she returned to the mosque. While she was washing from her menstruation, Jibril appeared to her in the form of a beardless young man, of radiant face, curly-haired and well-formed.

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him). It was also said that the "Spirit" is the spirit of ʿIsa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), and the attribution to Him is one of specification and honour. ﴿And he presented himself to her as a well-formed human being﴾, ﴿tamaththal﴾ meaning he took the appearance of a human being to her, ﴿bashaaran sawiyyan﴾, a complete human, with nothing lacking. He sent him in the form of a human so that Maryam (peace be upon her) would be steadied and able to listen to his speech. Had he come to her in his true form, she would have been terrified, fled from him, and been unable to hear his words.

When Maryam saw him, she said: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾, meaning a believer and obedient.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: she knew that the *taqi* (God-fearing) is one who possesses restraint (*nahyah*).

It was also said: there was a God-fearing man, among the most just people of that time. Maryam said: "If you are as righteous as the God-fearing man, then ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you﴾." How could a man who is a stranger and a woman who is a stranger be under one veil? Jibril said to her: ﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you﴾. That is, he says "to give you" (*li-ahaba*). Abu ʿAmr read *li-yahaba* with the *ya'* (a third-person form, "that He may give"), ﴿a pure boy﴾, righteous and God-fearing.

Maryam said: ﴿How can I have a boy when no human has touched me﴾, meaning no human has approached me, ﴿and I have not been unchaste﴾, meaning not immoral. The *ha'* was dropped from *bagiyyan* (unchaste) because the word is turned away from its usual form.

Jibril said: ﴿So it will be﴾, as you said, O Maryam. But ﴿your Lord said﴾, and it was also said: ﴿Thus your Lord said﴾. ﴿It is easy for Me﴾, meaning creating a child without a father. ﴿And that We may make him a sign﴾, an indication, ﴿to the people, and a mercy from Us﴾ to whoever follows him in his religion.

﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾, something enumerated and written in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*).

﴿So she conceived him﴾. That was because Jibril (peace be upon him) lifted her garment and blew into her collar, so she conceived when she put it on. It was also said: Jibril blew from a distance, and the wind reached her and she conceived. When she had conceived, ﴿she withdrew﴾, went out and isolated herself, ﴿to a remote place﴾, far from her family, beyond the mountain. It is said: at the far end of the house.

al-Kalbi said: it was said to a paternal cousin of hers named Yusuf: "Maryam has conceived from fornication," so that the king would kill her, for she had already been reported to him. He came to her and took her away, and fled with her. When they were on part of the road, Yusuf, her cousin, wanted to kill her. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "She is from the Holy Spirit, so do not kill her." So he left her, did not kill her, and remained with her.

They differed about the length of her pregnancy and the time of her delivery. Some said her pregnancy lasted nine months, like that of other women. Others said eight months, and that this was another sign, because no child born after eight months survived except ʿIsa. It was also said six months, and it was said three hours, and it was said one hour.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was only that she conceived and gave birth, and there was no interval between the conception and her withdrawal except one hour, because Allah, exalted is He, did not mention any separation between them.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: Maryam conceived him in an hour, he was formed in an hour, and she delivered him in an hour, when the sun had passed its zenith on that day. She was ten years old, and she had menstruated twice before she conceived ʿIsa.

﴿Then the pains of labour drove her﴾, meaning they forced her and brought her, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud): *awaha* (sheltered). That means the pregnancy, and it was also said: the labour pains.

﴿To the trunk of the palm tree﴾. It was a dry palm in the desert in the depth of winter, with no fronds.

Hilal ibn Khabbab narrated from Abu ʿUbaydullah: it was a dry trunk that had been brought to build with, a place called the House of Lahm (Bethlehem).

﴿She said: "Would that I had died before this, and had become a thing forgotten."﴾ Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read *nasyan* with a fathah on the *nun*, and the others read it with a kasrah. Both are dialect forms, like *al-watr* and *al-witr*, *al-hajr* and *al-hijr*, *al-jisr* and *al-jasr*, and it means a thing forgotten.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: meaning a thing abandoned. Qatadah said: a thing that is not remembered or known. ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: a discarded menstrual rag. al-Rabiʿ said: a miscarriage. Muqatil said: meaning like a destroyed thing. ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Muslim said: meaning one who was not created. al-Farraʾ said: it is what a woman throws away of the cloths used during her menstruation. Abu ʿUbayd said: it is what is forgotten and neglected of a trivial thing. al-Kumayt said:

*"Will you make us a bridge for the Kalb of Qudaʿah,*
*while we are not forgotten among Maʿadd nor an insignificant tribe?"*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/93.]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: "I wish that when I die I were a thing forgotten."

﴿Then he called her from beneath her﴾. al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *min tahtiha* with a kasrah on the *mim*, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him), who called to her from the foot of the mountain. The others read *man tahtaha* with a fathah on the *mim*, meaning ʿIsa, who, when he came out of her womb, called to her: ﴿Do not grieve, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾.

al-Hasan said: meaning ʿIsa. By Allah, he was a servant (*sariyy*), that is, noble. The other exegetes said it is a small stream. It was also said that the meaning of His words *tahtaki* (beneath you) is that Allah, exalted is He, placed the stream under her command: if she ordered it to flow, it flowed, and if she ordered it to stop, it stopped. This is like His words, related about Pharaoh: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾, meaning under my command. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Jibril struck the ground with his foot, or it is said ʿIsa struck the ground with his foot, and a spring of sweet water appeared and flowed. The palm tree, which had dried up, came back to life, put forth leaves, bore fruit, and produced ripe dates.

It was said to Maryam: ﴿And shake towards you﴾, that is, move, ﴿the trunk of the palm tree﴾. The Arabs say *hazzahu* and *hazza bihi*, as they say *khudh al-khitam* and *khudh bi-l-khitam* (take the halter), *ta'allaqa bi-Zayd* and *ta'allaqa Zaydan* (he clung to Zayd), *khudh ra'sahu* and *khudh bi-ra'sihi*, and *imdud al-habl* and *imdud bi-l-habl* (stretch the rope). The *jidhʿ* means a branch, and the *jidhʿ* also means the palm tree itself.

﴿It will drop upon you﴾. al-Bara ibn ʿAzib, Yaʿqub, Abu Hatim, Hammad and Nasir read *yusaqit* with a *ya'*. Hafs read *tusaqit* with a dammah on the *ta'*, a sukun on the *sin* and a kasrah on the *qaf*. al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and Abu ʿUbayd read *tassaqat* with a fathah on the *ta'* and the *qaf*, and a shaddah on the *sin*. Whoever read it feminine referred it to the palm, and whoever read it masculine referred it to the trunk. The shaddah indicates assimilation (*idghaam*), and the lightened form indicates deletion (*hadhf*).

﴿Ripe dates, fresh﴾, meaning a branch of moist dates, fresh at the time of picking.

al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym said: for a woman who has just given birth there is nothing better in my view than dates, and nothing better for a sick person than honey.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: I do not know of anything better for a woman whose child is difficult to deliver than dates, because of the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Shake towards you the trunk of the palm, it will drop upon you ripe dates, fresh﴾.

ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: it is among the Sunnah to chew dates and rub them on the mouth of a newborn. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to chew dates and rub them on the palate of the children of the Companions.

﴿So eat, O Maryam, and drink, and be comforted﴾, that is, let your eye be cool and your soul be at rest. ﴿And if you see any human, say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾, that is, silence. This is why it was read in the recitation of Ibn Masʿud and Anas as *sawm* (fast). In the language, *sawm* means abstaining from food and speech. There is an abridgement in the verse: ﴿If you see any human﴾ and he asks you about your child or blames you for it, ﴿then say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾. It is said that Allah commanded her to say this as a sign. It is also said that she was commanded to say it aloud, and then to remain silent after that.

﴿So I will not speak today to any human﴾. It is said: she used to speak with the angels and not speak with humans.

﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾. al-Kalbi said: Yusuf the carpenter took Maryam and her son ʿIsa (peace be upon him) to a cave and placed them in it for forty days until she was purified of her postnatal bleeding. Then he brought her out. ﴿She brought him﴾ means she brought ʿIsa, ﴿carrying him﴾, after forty days. ʿIsa spoke to her on the road and said: "O mother, be glad, for I am the servant of Allah and His Messiah." When she entered upon her family with the child, they wept and grieved, for they were a righteous household.

They said: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with a thing monstrous﴾, that is, grave, outrageous and enormous. Abu ʿUbaydah said: everything that is astonishing or is done is *fari*. The Prophet (ﷺ) said of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "I have not seen a *ʿabqari* who does his *fariyy*," meaning one who does his deed.

[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 12/232; Zad al-Masir: 5/159; Musnad Ahmad: 2/28, with variation.]

The rajaz poet said:

*"You have fed me sour old dates, one year old,*
*wormy, stiff, and hard,*
*and you have indeed been loud in praising them."*

Meaning: you have increased your speech about them and magnified them.

﴿O sister of Harun﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They meant Harun the Prophet, the brother of Musa, because she was of his lineage."

Qatadah and others said: Harun was a righteous man among the God-fearing of the Children of Israel, and he was not Harun the brother of Musa. It was reported to us that forty thousand people, all named Harun from the Children of Israel, followed his funeral when he died.

al-Mughirah ibn Shuʿbah said: the people of Najran said to me: "His words, ʿO sister of Harun,' and between Musa and ʿIsa there were what years there were." I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and the righteous who came before them?"

al-Kalbi said: Harun was the brother of Maryam from her father, not from her mother, and he was the most excellent man among the Children of Israel. It was also said: Harun was among the most immoral and most openly corrupt of the Children of Israel, so they likened her to him. According to this view, *ukht* (sister) here means likeness, not kinship, and the Arabs call the likeness of a thing its sister or brother. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning its likeness.

﴿Your father ʿImran was not a man of evil, nor was your mother Hannah unchaste﴾, meaning an adulteress. So from where did you get this child?

Then Maryam pointed to ʿIsa, telling them to speak to him. ﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾, that is, one who is in the cradle, meaning in her lap. It was also said: it is the cradle itself. The word was filler in speech and has no independent meaning, as in His words: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, meaning you are the best nation. Likewise His words: ﴿Was I not but a human messenger?﴾, meaning "Am I not?" And as people say: "If you are my friend, then join me." Zuhayr said:

*"She was ridden upon by a noble Arab mare,*
*when the night's colour was like the darkest black."*

Al-Farazdaq said:

*"How will it be when you see the abodes of my people,*
*and our noble neighbours?"*

Meaning: and our noble neighbours.

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/100; al-Tibyan: 7/123.]

Wahb said: Zakariyya came to her when she was debating the Jews, and said to ʿIsa: "Speak your proof, if you have been commanded to do so." Then ʿIsa said, at the age of forty days. Muqatil said: it was on the day he was born.

﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah."﴾ He acknowledged his servanthood to Allah, exalted is He, as the first thing he said, as a refutation of the Christians and as establishing the proof against them.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: when Maryam brought ʿIsa to her people, they picked up stones to stone her. When ʿIsa spoke, they left her. They said: then ʿIsa did not speak again after this until he became like other children.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Five spoke before the age of speech: the witness of Yusuf, the child of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, ʿIsa, the companion of Jurayj, and the child of the woman who was burned in the trench."

As for the witness of Yusuf, his mention has already passed. As for the child of the hairdresser:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance passed by him. He said: "O Jibril, what is this fragrance?" He said: "It is the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter. She was combing her hair when the comb fell from her hand, and she said: 'In the name of Allah.' Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'My father?' She said: 'No, but my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of your father.' She said: 'I will tell my father about that.' She said: 'Yes.' So she told him, and he summoned her and said: 'Who is your Lord?' She said: 'My Lord and your Lord is in heaven.' So Pharaoh ordered a cow of brass to be heated. He summoned her and her children and she said: 'I have a request of you.' He said: 'What is it?' She said: 'Gather my bones and the bones of my children and bury them together.' He said: 'That is due to you from us as a right.' So he ordered her children to be thrown in one by one, until the last of her children, who was a nursing infant. He said: 'Be patient, O mother, for we are upon the truth.' Then she was thrown in with her child."

As for the companion of Jurayj:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zaʿfarani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil told us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib told us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿAbd Allah [ibn Hamid] [in the Isfahan manuscript: Dawud] informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Rashid ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah told us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man called Jurayj was a monk who worshipped in his hermitage. His mother came to greet him and called out: 'O Jurayj, come to me, let me see you.' He was praying and said: 'My mother and my prayer are for my Lord.' He preferred his prayer to his Lord over his mother. She went away, then she came a second time and called: 'O Jurayj, speak to me.' He was praying and chose his prayer. Then she came a third time and he chose his prayer. She said: 'He refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of the prostitutes of Madinah.' He said: 'If she had prayed against him to be tested, he would have been tested.'"

He said: there was a shepherd of sheep who used to stay near his monastery. A woman from the village came, and he had intercourse with her, and she conceived and gave birth to a boy. She was asked: "Whose is this?" She said: "From the owner of the hermitage." So they came to him, demolished his hermitage, and took him away to their king. When he passed by the shops of the prostitutes, they came out, and he smiled, realizing that it was the supplication of his mother. They said: "Why did he laugh when he passed the prostitutes?" When he was brought before their king, Jurayj said: "Where is the child you have borne?" The child was brought, and Jurayj said to him: "Who is your father?" He said: "My father is so-and-so the shepherd." Then Allah, exalted is He, cleared Jurayj, and the people honoured him. They said: "We will build your monastery for you with gold and silver." He said: "No, but restore it as it was," and he went up to it.

As for the child of the woman of the trench, we will mention it in its place, if Allah wills.

﴿He has given me the Book﴾, meaning "He will give me the Book." Its form is past but its meaning is future. It was also said: he was informing about what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, as when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "When were you written as a prophet?" He said: "I was written a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body."

[Musnad Ahmad: 5/59.]

It was also said: the meaning is that He taught me and inspired me with the Torah while I was in my mother's womb.

﴿And He has made me a prophet, and made me blessed, wherever I am﴾, a teacher of good. It was also said: blessed to whoever follows my religion and my command. ﴿And He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah as long as I live, and dutiful to my mother﴾, meaning He made me dutiful toward my mother, ﴿and He has not made me a tyrant, unblessed.﴾

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 19, verses 16–40 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) giving life to the dead and healing the blind and the leper, among the signs that Allah had permitted him to perform. She said: "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast that nursed you." Ibn Maryam replied to her: "Blessed is the one who recites the Book of Allah and follows what is in it, and is not a tyrant or a wretch." He would also say: "Ask me, for my heart is soft and I am small in my own eyes, owing to the humility that Allah, glorified is He, has granted me."

﴿Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ ﴿That is 'Isa son of Maryam, a statement of truth,﴾ meaning: it is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is in the nominative by repetition, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, and that is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is an epithet of 'Isa, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, the Word of Allah, and "the truth" is Allah, glorified is He.

ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read qawla in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: he said the statement of truth ﴿about which they dispute﴾, meaning: they doubt and say what is untrue. The Jews said: "A sorcerer, a liar," and the Christians said: "The son of Allah" and "the third of three." Then He refuted them, saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾, meaning: it is not of His attributes to take a son. It was also said: the lam is transposed, meaning: Allah would not take a son; ﴿glory be to Him!﴾ He declared Himself free of it. ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ That is what was in His knowledge. ﴿And indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is the straight path.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿Indeed Allah﴾ with a kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnaf). ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, meaning: the Christians. They were called factions because they split into three groups concerning the matter of 'Isa: the Nestorians, the Melkites, and the Jacobites (al-Mar Ya'qubiyya).

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿How much they will hear and see!﴾ meaning: how much they will hear and see, in an expression of wonder. That is because they will hear on the Day of Resurrection when hearing will not benefit them, and they will see when sight will not benefit them.

al-Kalbi said: No one on the Day of Resurrection will hear or see more than them, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to 'Isa: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾ and so on.

﴿The day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided﴾, meaning: when the reckoning is finished, the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, and death has been slaughtered, ﴿while they are heedless﴾ of the world.
