When she menstruated, she moved to the house of her maternal aunt, and when she became pure again she returned to the mosque. While she was washing from her menstruation, Jibril appeared to her in the form of a beardless young man, of radiant face, curly-haired and well-formed.

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit﴾, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him). It was also said that the "Spirit" is the spirit of ʿIsa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), and the attribution to Him is one of specification and honour. ﴿And he presented himself to her as a well-formed human being﴾, ﴿tamaththal﴾ meaning he took the appearance of a human being to her, ﴿bashaaran sawiyyan﴾, a complete human, with nothing lacking. He sent him in the form of a human so that Maryam (peace be upon her) would be steadied and able to listen to his speech. Had he come to her in his true form, she would have been terrified, fled from him, and been unable to hear his words.

When Maryam saw him, she said: ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾, meaning a believer and obedient.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: she knew that the *taqi* (God-fearing) is one who possesses restraint (*nahyah*).

It was also said: there was a God-fearing man, among the most just people of that time. Maryam said: "If you are as righteous as the God-fearing man, then ﴿I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you﴾." How could a man who is a stranger and a woman who is a stranger be under one veil? Jibril said to her: ﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you﴾. That is, he says "to give you" (*li-ahaba*). Abu ʿAmr read *li-yahaba* with the *ya'* (a third-person form, "that He may give"), ﴿a pure boy﴾, righteous and God-fearing.

Maryam said: ﴿How can I have a boy when no human has touched me﴾, meaning no human has approached me, ﴿and I have not been unchaste﴾, meaning not immoral. The *ha'* was dropped from *bagiyyan* (unchaste) because the word is turned away from its usual form.

Jibril said: ﴿So it will be﴾, as you said, O Maryam. But ﴿your Lord said﴾, and it was also said: ﴿Thus your Lord said﴾. ﴿It is easy for Me﴾, meaning creating a child without a father. ﴿And that We may make him a sign﴾, an indication, ﴿to the people, and a mercy from Us﴾ to whoever follows him in his religion.

﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾, something enumerated and written in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*).

﴿So she conceived him﴾. That was because Jibril (peace be upon him) lifted her garment and blew into her collar, so she conceived when she put it on. It was also said: Jibril blew from a distance, and the wind reached her and she conceived. When she had conceived, ﴿she withdrew﴾, went out and isolated herself, ﴿to a remote place﴾, far from her family, beyond the mountain. It is said: at the far end of the house.

al-Kalbi said: it was said to a paternal cousin of hers named Yusuf: "Maryam has conceived from fornication," so that the king would kill her, for she had already been reported to him. He came to her and took her away, and fled with her. When they were on part of the road, Yusuf, her cousin, wanted to kill her. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "She is from the Holy Spirit, so do not kill her." So he left her, did not kill her, and remained with her.

They differed about the length of her pregnancy and the time of her delivery. Some said her pregnancy lasted nine months, like that of other women. Others said eight months, and that this was another sign, because no child born after eight months survived except ʿIsa. It was also said six months, and it was said three hours, and it was said one hour.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was only that she conceived and gave birth, and there was no interval between the conception and her withdrawal except one hour, because Allah, exalted is He, did not mention any separation between them.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: Maryam conceived him in an hour, he was formed in an hour, and she delivered him in an hour, when the sun had passed its zenith on that day. She was ten years old, and she had menstruated twice before she conceived ʿIsa.

﴿Then the pains of labour drove her﴾, meaning they forced her and brought her, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud): *awaha* (sheltered). That means the pregnancy, and it was also said: the labour pains.

﴿To the trunk of the palm tree﴾. It was a dry palm in the desert in the depth of winter, with no fronds.

Hilal ibn Khabbab narrated from Abu ʿUbaydullah: it was a dry trunk that had been brought to build with, a place called the House of Lahm (Bethlehem).

﴿She said: "Would that I had died before this, and had become a thing forgotten."﴾ Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read *nasyan* with a fathah on the *nun*, and the others read it with a kasrah. Both are dialect forms, like *al-watr* and *al-witr*, *al-hajr* and *al-hijr*, *al-jisr* and *al-jasr*, and it means a thing forgotten.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: meaning a thing abandoned. Qatadah said: a thing that is not remembered or known. ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: a discarded menstrual rag. al-Rabiʿ said: a miscarriage. Muqatil said: meaning like a destroyed thing. ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Muslim said: meaning one who was not created. al-Farraʾ said: it is what a woman throws away of the cloths used during her menstruation. Abu ʿUbayd said: it is what is forgotten and neglected of a trivial thing. al-Kumayt said:

*"Will you make us a bridge for the Kalb of Qudaʿah,*
*while we are not forgotten among Maʿadd nor an insignificant tribe?"*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/93.]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: "I wish that when I die I were a thing forgotten."

﴿Then he called her from beneath her﴾. al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, Nafiʿ, Ibn Wathhab, al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and al-Kisaʾi read *min tahtiha* with a kasrah on the *mim*, meaning Jibril (peace be upon him), who called to her from the foot of the mountain. The others read *man tahtaha* with a fathah on the *mim*, meaning ʿIsa, who, when he came out of her womb, called to her: ﴿Do not grieve, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾.

al-Hasan said: meaning ʿIsa. By Allah, he was a servant (*sariyy*), that is, noble. The other exegetes said it is a small stream. It was also said that the meaning of His words *tahtaki* (beneath you) is that Allah, exalted is He, placed the stream under her command: if she ordered it to flow, it flowed, and if she ordered it to stop, it stopped. This is like His words, related about Pharaoh: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾, meaning under my command. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Jibril struck the ground with his foot, or it is said ʿIsa struck the ground with his foot, and a spring of sweet water appeared and flowed. The palm tree, which had dried up, came back to life, put forth leaves, bore fruit, and produced ripe dates.

It was said to Maryam: ﴿And shake towards you﴾, that is, move, ﴿the trunk of the palm tree﴾. The Arabs say *hazzahu* and *hazza bihi*, as they say *khudh al-khitam* and *khudh bi-l-khitam* (take the halter), *ta'allaqa bi-Zayd* and *ta'allaqa Zaydan* (he clung to Zayd), *khudh ra'sahu* and *khudh bi-ra'sihi*, and *imdud al-habl* and *imdud bi-l-habl* (stretch the rope). The *jidhʿ* means a branch, and the *jidhʿ* also means the palm tree itself.

﴿It will drop upon you﴾. al-Bara ibn ʿAzib, Yaʿqub, Abu Hatim, Hammad and Nasir read *yusaqit* with a *ya'*. Hafs read *tusaqit* with a dammah on the *ta'*, a sukun on the *sin* and a kasrah on the *qaf*. al-Aʿmash, Hamzah and Abu ʿUbayd read *tassaqat* with a fathah on the *ta'* and the *qaf*, and a shaddah on the *sin*. Whoever read it feminine referred it to the palm, and whoever read it masculine referred it to the trunk. The shaddah indicates assimilation (*idghaam*), and the lightened form indicates deletion (*hadhf*).

﴿Ripe dates, fresh﴾, meaning a branch of moist dates, fresh at the time of picking.

al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym said: for a woman who has just given birth there is nothing better in my view than dates, and nothing better for a sick person than honey.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: I do not know of anything better for a woman whose child is difficult to deliver than dates, because of the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Shake towards you the trunk of the palm, it will drop upon you ripe dates, fresh﴾.

ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: it is among the Sunnah to chew dates and rub them on the mouth of a newborn. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to chew dates and rub them on the palate of the children of the Companions.

﴿So eat, O Maryam, and drink, and be comforted﴾, that is, let your eye be cool and your soul be at rest. ﴿And if you see any human, say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾, that is, silence. This is why it was read in the recitation of Ibn Masʿud and Anas as *sawm* (fast). In the language, *sawm* means abstaining from food and speech. There is an abridgement in the verse: ﴿If you see any human﴾ and he asks you about your child or blames you for it, ﴿then say: "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾. It is said that Allah commanded her to say this as a sign. It is also said that she was commanded to say it aloud, and then to remain silent after that.

﴿So I will not speak today to any human﴾. It is said: she used to speak with the angels and not speak with humans.

﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾. al-Kalbi said: Yusuf the carpenter took Maryam and her son ʿIsa (peace be upon him) to a cave and placed them in it for forty days until she was purified of her postnatal bleeding. Then he brought her out. ﴿She brought him﴾ means she brought ʿIsa, ﴿carrying him﴾, after forty days. ʿIsa spoke to her on the road and said: "O mother, be glad, for I am the servant of Allah and His Messiah." When she entered upon her family with the child, they wept and grieved, for they were a righteous household.

They said: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with a thing monstrous﴾, that is, grave, outrageous and enormous. Abu ʿUbaydah said: everything that is astonishing or is done is *fari*. The Prophet (ﷺ) said of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "I have not seen a *ʿabqari* who does his *fariyy*," meaning one who does his deed.

[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 12/232; Zad al-Masir: 5/159; Musnad Ahmad: 2/28, with variation.]

The rajaz poet said:

*"You have fed me sour old dates, one year old,*
*wormy, stiff, and hard,*
*and you have indeed been loud in praising them."*

Meaning: you have increased your speech about them and magnified them.

﴿O sister of Harun﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They meant Harun the Prophet, the brother of Musa, because she was of his lineage."

Qatadah and others said: Harun was a righteous man among the God-fearing of the Children of Israel, and he was not Harun the brother of Musa. It was reported to us that forty thousand people, all named Harun from the Children of Israel, followed his funeral when he died.

al-Mughirah ibn Shuʿbah said: the people of Najran said to me: "His words, ʿO sister of Harun,' and between Musa and ʿIsa there were what years there were." I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and the righteous who came before them?"

al-Kalbi said: Harun was the brother of Maryam from her father, not from her mother, and he was the most excellent man among the Children of Israel. It was also said: Harun was among the most immoral and most openly corrupt of the Children of Israel, so they likened her to him. According to this view, *ukht* (sister) here means likeness, not kinship, and the Arabs call the likeness of a thing its sister or brother. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning its likeness.

﴿Your father ʿImran was not a man of evil, nor was your mother Hannah unchaste﴾, meaning an adulteress. So from where did you get this child?

Then Maryam pointed to ʿIsa, telling them to speak to him. ﴿They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾, that is, one who is in the cradle, meaning in her lap. It was also said: it is the cradle itself. The word was filler in speech and has no independent meaning, as in His words: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, meaning you are the best nation. Likewise His words: ﴿Was I not but a human messenger?﴾, meaning "Am I not?" And as people say: "If you are my friend, then join me." Zuhayr said:

*"She was ridden upon by a noble Arab mare,*
*when the night's colour was like the darkest black."*

Al-Farazdaq said:

*"How will it be when you see the abodes of my people,*
*and our noble neighbours?"*

Meaning: and our noble neighbours.

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/100; al-Tibyan: 7/123.]

Wahb said: Zakariyya came to her when she was debating the Jews, and said to ʿIsa: "Speak your proof, if you have been commanded to do so." Then ʿIsa said, at the age of forty days. Muqatil said: it was on the day he was born.

﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah."﴾ He acknowledged his servanthood to Allah, exalted is He, as the first thing he said, as a refutation of the Christians and as establishing the proof against them.

ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: when Maryam brought ʿIsa to her people, they picked up stones to stone her. When ʿIsa spoke, they left her. They said: then ʿIsa did not speak again after this until he became like other children.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Five spoke before the age of speech: the witness of Yusuf, the child of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, ʿIsa, the companion of Jurayj, and the child of the woman who was burned in the trench."

As for the witness of Yusuf, his mention has already passed. As for the child of the hairdresser:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, a pleasant fragrance passed by him. He said: "O Jibril, what is this fragrance?" He said: "It is the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter. She was combing her hair when the comb fell from her hand, and she said: 'In the name of Allah.' Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'My father?' She said: 'No, but my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of your father.' She said: 'I will tell my father about that.' She said: 'Yes.' So she told him, and he summoned her and said: 'Who is your Lord?' She said: 'My Lord and your Lord is in heaven.' So Pharaoh ordered a cow of brass to be heated. He summoned her and her children and she said: 'I have a request of you.' He said: 'What is it?' She said: 'Gather my bones and the bones of my children and bury them together.' He said: 'That is due to you from us as a right.' So he ordered her children to be thrown in one by one, until the last of her children, who was a nursing infant. He said: 'Be patient, O mother, for we are upon the truth.' Then she was thrown in with her child."

As for the companion of Jurayj:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zaʿfarani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil told us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Muʾaddib told us, saying: al-Layth ibn Saʿd told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And ʿAbd Allah [ibn Hamid] [in the Isfahan manuscript: Dawud] informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Rashid ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah told us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Rafiʿ, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man called Jurayj was a monk who worshipped in his hermitage. His mother came to greet him and called out: 'O Jurayj, come to me, let me see you.' He was praying and said: 'My mother and my prayer are for my Lord.' He preferred his prayer to his Lord over his mother. She went away, then she came a second time and called: 'O Jurayj, speak to me.' He was praying and chose his prayer. Then she came a third time and he chose his prayer. She said: 'He refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of the prostitutes of Madinah.' He said: 'If she had prayed against him to be tested, he would have been tested.'"

He said: there was a shepherd of sheep who used to stay near his monastery. A woman from the village came, and he had intercourse with her, and she conceived and gave birth to a boy. She was asked: "Whose is this?" She said: "From the owner of the hermitage." So they came to him, demolished his hermitage, and took him away to their king. When he passed by the shops of the prostitutes, they came out, and he smiled, realizing that it was the supplication of his mother. They said: "Why did he laugh when he passed the prostitutes?" When he was brought before their king, Jurayj said: "Where is the child you have borne?" The child was brought, and Jurayj said to him: "Who is your father?" He said: "My father is so-and-so the shepherd." Then Allah, exalted is He, cleared Jurayj, and the people honoured him. They said: "We will build your monastery for you with gold and silver." He said: "No, but restore it as it was," and he went up to it.

As for the child of the woman of the trench, we will mention it in its place, if Allah wills.

﴿He has given me the Book﴾, meaning "He will give me the Book." Its form is past but its meaning is future. It was also said: he was informing about what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, as when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "When were you written as a prophet?" He said: "I was written a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body."

[Musnad Ahmad: 5/59.]

It was also said: the meaning is that He taught me and inspired me with the Torah while I was in my mother's womb.

﴿And He has made me a prophet, and made me blessed, wherever I am﴾, a teacher of good. It was also said: blessed to whoever follows my religion and my command. ﴿And He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah as long as I live, and dutiful to my mother﴾, meaning He made me dutiful toward my mother, ﴿and He has not made me a tyrant, unblessed.﴾

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying:

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 19, verses 16–40 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) giving life to the dead and healing the blind and the leper, among the signs that Allah had permitted him to perform. She said: "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast that nursed you." Ibn Maryam replied to her: "Blessed is the one who recites the Book of Allah and follows what is in it, and is not a tyrant or a wretch." He would also say: "Ask me, for my heart is soft and I am small in my own eyes, owing to the humility that Allah, glorified is He, has granted me."

﴿Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.﴾ ﴿That is 'Isa son of Maryam, a statement of truth,﴾ meaning: it is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is in the nominative by repetition, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, and that is the statement of truth. It was also said: it is an epithet of 'Isa, meaning: that is 'Isa son of Maryam, the Word of Allah, and "the truth" is Allah, glorified is He.

ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read qawla in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: he said the statement of truth ﴿about which they dispute﴾, meaning: they doubt and say what is untrue. The Jews said: "A sorcerer, a liar," and the Christians said: "The son of Allah" and "the third of three." Then He refuted them, saying: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾, meaning: it is not of His attributes to take a son. It was also said: the lam is transposed, meaning: Allah would not take a son; ﴿glory be to Him!﴾ He declared Himself free of it. ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ That is what was in His knowledge. ﴿And indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is the straight path.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿Indeed Allah﴾ with a kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnaf). ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, meaning: the Christians. They were called factions because they split into three groups concerning the matter of 'Isa: the Nestorians, the Melkites, and the Jacobites (al-Mar Ya'qubiyya).

﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a great day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. ﴿How much they will hear and see!﴾ meaning: how much they will hear and see, in an expression of wonder. That is because they will hear on the Day of Resurrection when hearing will not benefit them, and they will see when sight will not benefit them.

al-Kalbi said: No one on the Day of Resurrection will hear or see more than them, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to 'Isa: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾ and so on.

﴿The day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided﴾, meaning: when the reckoning is finished, the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, and death has been slaughtered, ﴿while they are heedless﴾ of the world.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan narrated to us, saying: [In the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warraq, from ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah, from] ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Saʿid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white-speckled ram. It will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?' They will crane their necks and look and say: 'Yes, this is Death.' It will be commanded and slaughtered. Then a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death! O people of the Fire, eternity without death!' So the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in sorrow upon their sorrow." [In the Isfahan manuscript: "It will be slaughtered, and it will be said."] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And warn them of the day of regret, when the matter is decided, while they are in heedlessness﴾, and he pointed with his hand toward the world. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/9, with variation.]

Muqatil said: Were it not for what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, decreed concerning the eternal abiding of the people of the Fire and their remaining in it, they would die of regret when they saw that.

﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾, meaning: We cause them to die, and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, remains, and He inherits them. ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾, so We will recompense them for their deeds.

It is also said the meaning is: I fear that He will send down upon you a punishment in this world, ﴿so you would be an ally of Satan﴾, a companion in the Fire.

His father replied to him: ﴿Do you turn away from my gods, O Ibrahim?﴾, that is, do you abandon their worship and renounce them? ﴿If you do not desist﴾, that is, if you do not stop and withdraw from your speech, ﴿I will surely stone you﴾. Al-Dahhak, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: I will surely revile you. Ibn Abbas said: I will surely strike you. It is also said: I will surely expose your affair. ﴿And leave me for a long time﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ata said: safe. Ibn Abbas said: and withdraw from me, safe in honor, no harm from me will reach you. Al-Kalbi said: leave me and keep away from me for a long time, so do not speak to me. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: a long age. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: a while. The root of the word is staying, and from it one says: "I stayed a while" (tamallaytu ḥīnan). Al-Mulawan are the night and the day.

Ibrahim said: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾, that is, you are safe from me, I will not harm you with anything disliked. ﴿I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you; indeed, He is ever gracious to me﴾. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: kind and merciful. It is also said: righteous. Mujahid said: He accustomed me to answering. Al-Kalbi said: knowing, who responds to me when I call upon Him.

Al-Kalbi said: wealth and children. It is also said: prophethood and the Book. Its clarification is His words: ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [[Surah al-Zukhruf: 32.]]

﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, elevated﴾, meaning a good and lofty commendation among all the people of the religions, and every people of a religion will take them as allies and praise them.

And mention in the Book Musa. He was ﹟sincere (mukhlaṣan), meaning not showing off. Muqatil [in the Isfahan copy: Qatadah] said: a Muslim who affirms the oneness of God. The people of Kufa read mukhlaṣan with a fathah on the lam, meaning We purified him and chose him. ﴿And he was a messenger, a prophet﴾. ﴿And We called him﴾, that is, We summoned him and spoke to him, on the night of Friday, ﴿from the right side of the mountain﴾, meaning the right side of Musa. Al-Ṭūr (the mountain) is a mountain between Egypt and Madyan. ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾, meaning We raised him from heaven to heaven and from veil to veil, until there was between him and Him only one veil.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar informed us, saying: Asbat informed us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Maysarah, concerning ﴿and brought him near as a confidant﴾: He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen. The najī is the one who converses in confidence, like a companion or a boon-companion.

And Allah answered his supplication.

And mention in the Book Isma'il, meaning the son of Ibrahim. ﴿He was true to his promise﴾: whenever he promised, he fulfilled it. That was because he promised a man that he would remain in his place until the man returned to him, so Isma'il remained in his place three days for the appointed time until the man returned to him. Muqatil said this, and al-Kalbi said: he waited for him until a full year passed over him. ﴿And he was a messenger to his people, a prophet﴾, reporting from Allah, glorified is He.

﴿And he used to enjoin on his family﴾, meaning his people. Likewise, it is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿prayer and zakah﴾. ﴿And he was with his Lord, pleasing﴾, that is, righteous and pure.

And mention in the Book Ibrahim. He was truthful (ṣiddīq), a believer, certain in faith, very truthful, a prophet, a messenger, and exalted. When he said to his father Azar, who worshipped idols:

﴿Why do you worship what neither hears nor sees, and cannot benefit you or avail you anything?﴾

That is, the idols. "O my father, there has come to me of knowledge and clear proof what has not come to you. So follow me in my religion, and I will guide you to a straight path, upright and even."

﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful.﴾ Do not obey him. You did not pray to him or fast for him. Whoever obeys something has worshipped it. Here "kāna" means the present state, that is, "he is." It is also said it means "became."

﴿O my father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will afflict you﴾, meaning I know that it will afflict you, as in His words, ﴿unless they both fear﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 229.]] and His words, ﴿if you fear that they will not keep within the limits﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 229.]]. It is also said the meaning is: I fear that He will send down upon you a punishment in this world, ﴿so you would be an ally of Satan﴾, a companion in the Fire.

His father replied to him: ﴿Do you turn away from my gods, O Ibrahim?﴾, that is, do you abandon their worship and renounce them? ﴿If you do not desist﴾, that is, if you do not stop and withdraw from your speech, ﴿I will surely stone you﴾. Al-Dahhak, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: I will surely revile you. Ibn Abbas said: I will surely strike you. It is also said: I will surely expose your affair. ﴿And leave me for a long time﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ata said: safe. Ibn Abbas said: and withdraw from me, safe in honor, no harm from me will reach you. Al-Kalbi said: leave me and keep away from me for a long time, so do not speak to me. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: a long age. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: a while. The root of the word is staying, and from it one says: "I stayed a while" (tamallaytu ḥīnan). Al-Mulawan are the night and the day.

Ibrahim said: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾, that is, you are safe from me, I will not harm you with anything disliked. ﴿I will ask my Lord for forgiveness for you; indeed, He is ever gracious to me﴾. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: kind and merciful. It is also said: righteous. Mujahid said: He accustomed me to answering. Al-Kalbi said: knowing, who responds to me when I call upon Him.

﴿And I will leave you and what you call upon other than Allah﴾, meaning I will leave what you worship other than Allah. Muqatil said: His withdrawal from them was that he parted from them at Kuthā and emigrated from it to the Holy Land.

﴿And I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I will not be in vain in my supplication to my Lord﴾, meaning perhaps He will answer me and not disappoint me. And mention in the Book Idris; indeed he was a truthful man, a prophet. [Note: translating faithfully below.]

Actually, I must give the translation only, without notes. Here it is:

And mention in the Book Idris. He was the grandfather of Nuh's father, and he was named Idris for his great study of books (dars). His name was Akhnukh, and he was a tailor. He was the first to write with the pen, the first to sew garments and wear stitched clothing, and the first to speak on the science of the stars and calculation. Indeed he was a man of truth (siddiq), a prophet, and We raised him to a high station, meaning Paradise.

Al-Dahhak said: He was raised to the sixth heaven. It was also said: the fourth.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi informed us, both saying: Makki ibn Abdan al-Tamimi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning His words "and We raised him to a high station," he said: Anas ibn Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah told us that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was taken up to the heaven, said: "I came upon Idris in the heaven: the fourth." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 5/293.] ...

The cause of his being raised, according to what Ibn Abbas, Ka'b and others said, was that he walked one day on an errand, and the heat of the sun struck him, and he said: "O Lord, I walked one day, so how about one who carries it for five hundred years in a single day? O God, lighten its weight from him and bear its heat for him." When the angel woke in the morning, he found from the lightness and heat of the sun what was unknown. He said: "O Lord, You created me to carry the sun; what have You decreed for it?" He said: "As for My servant Idris, he asked Me to lighten its burden and heat for you, and I answered him." He said: "O Lord, bring me together with him and make a friendship between me and him." Permission was given to him, and he came to Idris, who was asking him questions. Among what he asked was: "I have been told that you are the most honored of the angels and the most influential with the Angel of Death. So intercede for me with him that he delay my term," so that he would increase in gratitude and worship. The angel said: "God does not delay a soul when its term comes." He said: "I know that, but it is more comforting to my soul." He said: "Yes, I will speak to him for you; whatever he could do for any of the sons of Adam, he will do for you." Then the angel of the sun carried him on his wing, raised him to the heaven, and placed him at the rising place of the sun. Then he came to the Angel of Death and said: "I have a need of you." He said: "I will do anything I am able to." He said: "A friend of mine from the sons of Adam seeks your intercession with you that you delay his term." He said: "That is not up to me, but if you wish, I will inform him of his term, when he will die, so that he may prepare himself." He said: "Yes." So he looked in his register and informed him of his name, and said: "You spoke to me about a man whom I do not see dying ever." He said: "How so?" He said: "I do not find him dying except at the rising of the sun." He said: "I came to you and left him there." He said: "Go, for I do not think you will find him except that he has died." By God, nothing remained of Idris's term, and the angel returned and found him dead.

Wahb said: Each day there was raised for Idris worship equal to what was raised for all the people of the earth in his time, and the angels marvelled at him, and the Angel of Death longed to meet him. He asked his Lord permission to visit him, and it was granted. He came to him in the form of a son of Adam. Idris was fasting, observing the fast of the whole year. When it was time for his breaking of the fast, he invited him to his food, but he refused to eat with him. This happened for three nights, and Idris disapproved of it. On the third night he said to him: "I want to know who you are." He said: "I am the Angel of Death; I asked my Lord to accompany you, and He permitted me." He said: "Then I have a need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Take my soul." God, mighty and majestic, revealed to him: "Take his soul," so he took his soul, and God returned it to him after an hour.

The Angel of Death said to him: "What is the benefit of your asking me to take the soul?" He said: "That I may taste the anguish and distress of death, so that I may be more prepared for it." Then Idris said to him: "I have another need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Raise me to the heaven so that I may look at it, and at the Garden and the Fire." God permitted him to raise him to the heavens. When he drew near the Fire, he said: "A need." He said: "What do you want?" He said: "Ask Malik to open its gate for me so I may return." He did so. Then he said: "Just as you showed me the Fire, show me the Garden." He took him to the Garden, asked for entry, and its gates were opened, and he entered him into the Garden. Then the Angel of Death said to him: "Come out, that you may return to your abode." But he clung to a tree and said: "I will not come out of it." So God sent an angel as judge between them, to consider their words. The angel said to him: "Why will you not come out?" He said: "Because God, exalted, said: 'Every soul shall taste death' [Al 'Imran: 85], and I have tasted it; and He said: 'There is none of you but will come to it' [Maryam: 71], and I have come to it; and He said: 'They will not be removed from it' [al-Hijr: 48], so I will not come out." God, glorified, revealed to the Angel of Death: "Enter the Garden, and by My command he will come out." He is alive there, and that is His words: "and We raised him to a high station."

Those are the ones upon whom God bestowed favor among the prophets of the offspring of Adam, and of those whom We carried with Nuh in the ark, and of the offspring of Ibrahim and Isra'il, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping. "Bukiyyan" is the plural of "baki," its form from the verb being fu'ul, like sajid and sujud, rak' and ruku', qa'id and qu'ud, pluralized on the form of the verbal noun. It was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book, Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions.

Then there succeeded after them, meaning after the aforementioned prophets, a successor (khalf) of evil people. "Khalaf" with a fatha is the righteous, "khalf" with a sukun on the lam is the wicked, and "khalf" with a sukun on the lam is the bad of anything. In this verse they are the Jews and those who joined them. Mujahid and Qatadah said: it refers to this Community.

They neglected the prayer, meaning they abandoned the obligatory prayers. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibrahim and al-Qasim ibn Makhimarah said: they delayed them beyond their appointed times and prayed them outside their time.

Qurrah ibn Khalid said: al-Dahhak once delayed the afternoon prayer in doubt until the sun almost set, then recited this verse, "They neglected the prayer," and then said: "By God, if I leave it, that is dearer to me than that I should neglect it." Al-Hasan recited "adā'ū al-ṣalawāt" (they lost the prayers). Muqatil said: they made lawful marriage to a sister from the father's side. Al-Kalbi said: it means pleasures, drinking wine, and other things. Mujahid said: this is at the approach of the Hour and the passing of the righteous of the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ), when some of them leap upon others in the lanes and alleys as fornicators.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning this verse, that he said: "There will come a successor after sixty years, who neglect the prayer and follow the passions," and the verse [Musnad Ahmad: 3/38.]

Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "This is when lofty buildings are built, the visible (mounts) are ridden, and the famous garments are worn."

Wahb said: "There succeeded after them a successor who drink the coffees, play with the cubes, ride the passions, follow pleasures, abandon the Friday prayers [in the Isfahan copy: the congregations], and neglect the prayers." Ka'b said: "At the end of time there will appear people with whips in their hands like cows' tails, striking people," then he recited, "There succeeded after them a successor; they neglected the prayer and followed the passions."

So they will meet error (ghayy). Ibn Mas'ud said: "Al-Ghayy is a fire [in the Isfahan copy: a river] in Hell." Ibn Abbas said: "Al-Ghayy is a valley in Hell, and the valleys of Hell seek refuge from its heat. It is prepared for the fornicator who persists in it, the wine-drinker who is addicted to it, the eater of usury who does not desist from it, the people of disobedience to parents, the false witness, and a woman who introduced a child into her husband's household." Ata said: "Al-Ghayy is a valley in Hell that flows with pus and blood." Wahb said: "Al-Ghayy is a river in the Fire, deep in its bottom and foul in its taste." Ka'b said: "It is a valley in Hell, the deepest in its bottom and the most intense in its heat; in it is a well called al-Buhaym, whenever Hell subsides God opens that well and Hell is kindled by it." Al-Dahhak said: "Loss; and it was said: punishment; and it was said: pain; and it was said: disbelief."

Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds; those will enter the Garden and will not be wronged in the least. Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen, though they have not seen them. Indeed His promise is ever coming, meaning "ātiyan" (coming). Al-A'sha said:

"And I was walking with one disobedient toward her, and her goader."

That is, "'āṣiyan" (disobedient).

They will not hear therein, in the Garden, any vain talk (laghw), falsehood, obscenity, or superfluous speech. Muqatil said: "a false oath." Except "salaman" (peace), an exception from other than its kind, meaning they will hear therein only peace, that is, speech from which they are safe. The commentators said: this means their greeting one another, and the greeting of the angels to them. And for them their provision therein morning and evening, meaning in measure of the two ends of the day.

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far informed us, reading to him, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sakhtawayh told us, saying: Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-Darir told us, saying: Amdh ibn Siyaq told us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: In their time the Arabs considered one who had a lunch with a dinner to be a man of ease. So God revealed, "And for them their provision therein morning and evening," the measure between their lunch and dinner.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sakhtawayh told us, saying: Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Dawud ibn Rashid told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: I asked Zuhayr ibn Muhammad about God's words, "And for them their provision therein morning and evening," and he said: "There is no night in the Garden; they are always in light, and they know the measure of night only by the lowering of the veils, and the measure of day by the raising of the veils."

That is the Garden which We will cause to inherit from Our servants who were God-fearing. Ya'qub recited "nuwarrithu" with doubling, but the preferred reading is the lighter, because of His words, "Then We caused to inherit" [al-Fatir: 32]. "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord" [Maryam: 64], the verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ['Muhammad ibn' in the Isfahan copy] Abdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh ibn Ubadah told us, saying: Umar ibn Dharr told us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, what prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?" So God revealed, "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord."

Mujahid said: The messengers were delayed from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then Jibril came to him, and he said: "What detained you?" He said: "How could we come to you when you do not trim your nails, nor take your mustaches, nor use the siwak?" [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/137.] So God revealed, "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord," the verse.

Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil, Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: Jibril was held back from the Prophet (ﷺ) when his people asked him about the story of the People of the Cave, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, and he did not know how to answer them, hoping that Jibril would bring him the answer to what they asked, but he was delayed. Ikrimah said: forty days. Mujahid said: twelve nights. It was also said: fifteen. This was a severe hardship upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and abandoned him." When Jibril came down, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "You delayed me until my opinion grew bad and I longed for you." Jibril said to him: "I used to long for you more, but I am a servant under command: when I am sent I descend, and when I am held back I am held back." So God, exalted, revealed, "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord," and He revealed, "By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you" [al-Duha: 1-3].

It was also said: this is information about the people of the Garden, that they say upon entering it: "These gardens do not descend except by the command of God." "To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us, and what is between that." Muqatil said: to Him belongs what is before us of the affairs of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of the affairs of this world, and what is between that, meaning between the two blasts, and between them is forty years. It was also said: to Him belongs the beginning of our creation, and to Him belongs the end of our terms, and to Him belongs the duration of our lives.

It is said: "What is before us" is the reward and punishment and the matters of the Hereafter; "what is behind us" is what has passed of our deeds in this world; "what is between that" is what will happen from us until the Day of Resurrection. It is said: "to Him belongs what is before us" before He creates us, "and what is behind us" after He makes us die, "and what is between that" is what we are in of life. It is said: "to Him belongs what is before us" up to the earth when we want to descend to it, "and what is behind us," that is, the heaven when we descend from it, "and what is between that," meaning the heaven and the earth, intending that all of that belongs to God, glorified, so none of us is able to do anything except by His command.

"And your Lord was never forgetful" — that is, forgetful: when He wishes to send to you, He sends. "Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship" — that is, be patient in His worship. "Do you know anyone worthy of His name?" Ibn Abbas said: "a like." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "an equal." Al-Kalbi said: "Do you know anyone called God other than Him?"

"And man says: 'When I die, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?'" — meaning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, mockingly and denying resurrection.

God, glorified, said: "Does man not remember," that is, recall and reflect; the root is "yatadhakkar." Ibn Amir, Nafi', 'Asim and Ya'qub read "yadhkuru" with lightness, but the preferred reading is with doubling, because of His words, "Only those of understanding remember" [al-Ra'd: 19], and its like, and it is supported by Ubayy's reading "yatadhakkaru al-insan." Man, meaning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, that "We created him before, and he was nothing." Then He swore by Himself, saying, "So by your Lord, We will surely gather them," that is, gather them for the Return, meaning the polytheists who deny resurrection, "and the devils with them," meaning their companions who misled them, each disbeliever being bound in a chain with a devil. "Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell," that is, within Hell, "on their knees." Ibn Abbas said: "groups upon groups." Muqatil said: "all together," and on this view it is the plural of "juthwah." Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: "kneeling on their knees," and on this interpretation it is the plural of "jathin." Al-Kumayt said:

"They left their nobles kneeling, while they were humbled beneath the nobles."

"Then We will surely draw out from every faction," that is, bring out from every community and religion, "whichever of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful." Ibn Abbas said: "that is, audacity." Mujahid said: "wickedness and lying." Muqatil said: "haughtiness." It was said: "extremism in disbelief," and it was said: "disbelief." Al-Kalbi said: "their leader is their chief in evil."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali told us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from Sufyan, from Ali ibn al-Aqram, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: "We begin with the greatest, then the greatest." "Then indeed We are most knowing of those most deserving of entering it [the Fire]," that is, most worthy of entry into the Fire. It is said: "saliya yuslaa saliyyan," like "laqiya yalqa laqiyyan," and "salā yaṣlā ṣaliyyan," like "mada yamdi madiyyan."

He said: "O Lord, You created me to carry the sun; what have You decreed for it?" He said: "As for My servant Idris, he asked Me to lighten its burden and heat for you, and I answered him." He said: "O Lord, bring me together with him and make a friendship between me and him." Permission was given to him, and he came to Idris, who was asking him questions. Among what he asked was: "I have been told that you are the most honored of the angels and the most influential with the Angel of Death. So intercede for me with him that he delay my term," so that he would increase in gratitude and worship. The angel said: "God does not delay a soul when its term comes." He said: "I know that, but it is more comforting to my soul." He said: "Yes, I will speak to him for you; whatever he could do for any of the sons of Adam, he will do for you." Then the angel of the sun carried him on his wing, raised him to the heaven, and placed him at the rising place of the sun. Then he came to the Angel of Death and said: "I have a need of you." He said: "I will do anything I am able to." He said: "A friend of mine from the sons of Adam seeks your intercession with you that you delay his term." He said: "That is not up to me, but if you wish, I will inform him of his term, when he will die, so that he may prepare himself." He said: "Yes." So he looked in his register and informed him of his name, and said: "You spoke to me about a man whom I do not see dying ever." He said: "How so?" He said: "I do not find him dying except at the rising of the sun." He said: "I came to you and left him there." He said: "Go, for I do not think you will find him except that he has died." By God, nothing remained of Idris's term, and the angel returned and found him dead.

Wahb said: Each day there was raised for Idris worship equal to what was raised for all the people of the earth in his time, and the angels marvelled at him, and the Angel of Death longed to meet him. He asked his Lord permission to visit him, and it was granted. He came to him in the form of a son of Adam. Idris was fasting, observing the fast of the whole year. When it was time for his breaking of the fast, he invited him to his food, but he refused to eat with him. This happened for three nights, and Idris disapproved of it. On the third night he said to him: "I want to know who you are." He said: "I am the Angel of Death; I asked my Lord to accompany you, and He permitted me." He said: "Then I have a need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Take my soul." God, mighty and majestic, revealed to him: "Take his soul," so he took his soul, and God returned it to him after an hour.

The Angel of Death said to him: "What is the benefit of your asking me to take the soul?" He said: "That I may taste the anguish and distress of death, so that I may be more prepared for it." Then Idris said to him: "I have another need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Raise me to the heaven so that I may look at it, and at the Garden and the Fire." God permitted him to raise him to the heavens. When he drew near the Fire, he said: "A need." He said: "What do you want?" He said: "Ask Malik to open its gate for me so I may return." He did so. Then he said: "Just as you showed me the Fire, show me the Garden." He took him to the Garden, asked for entry, and its gates were opened, and he entered him into the Garden. Then the Angel of Death said to him: "Come out, that you may return to your abode." But he clung to a tree and said: "I will not come out of it." So God sent an angel as judge between them, to consider their words. The angel said to him: "Why will you not come out?" He said: "Because God, exalted, said: 'Every soul shall taste death' [Al 'Imran: 85], and I have tasted it; and He said: 'There is none of you but will come to it' [Maryam: 71], and I have come to it; and He said: 'They will not be removed from it' [al-Hijr: 48], so I will not come out." God, glorified, revealed to the Angel of Death: "Enter the Garden, and by My command he will come out." He is alive there, and that is His words: "and We raised him to a high station."

Those are the ones upon whom God bestowed favor among the prophets of the offspring of Adam, and of those whom We carried with Nuh in the ark, and of the offspring of Ibrahim and Isra'il, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping. "Bukiyyan" is the plural of "baki," its form from the verb being fu'ul, like sajid and sujud, rak' and ruku', qa'id and qu'ud, pluralized on the form of the verbal noun. It was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book, Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions.

Then there succeeded after them, meaning after the aforementioned prophets, a successor (khalf) of evil people. "Khalaf" with a fatha is the righteous, "khalf" with a sukun on the lam is the wicked, and "khalf" with a sukun on the lam is the bad of anything. In this verse they are the Jews and those who joined them. Mujahid and Qatadah said: it refers to this Community.

They neglected the prayer, meaning they abandoned the obligatory prayers. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibrahim and al-Qasim ibn Makhimarah said: they delayed them beyond their appointed times and prayed them outside their time.

Qurrah ibn Khalid said: al-Dahhak once delayed the afternoon prayer in doubt until the sun almost set, then recited this verse, "They neglected the prayer," and then said: "By God, if I leave it, that is dearer to me than that I should neglect it." Al-Hasan recited "adā'ū al-ṣalawāt" (they lost the prayers). Muqatil said: they made lawful marriage to a sister from the father's side. Al-Kalbi said: it means pleasures, drinking wine, and other things. Mujahid said: this is at the approach of the Hour and the passing of the righteous of the Community of Muhammad (ﷺ), when some of them leap upon others in the lanes and alleys as fornicators.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) concerning this verse, that he said: "There will come a successor after sixty years, who neglect the prayer and follow the passions," and the verse [Musnad Ahmad: 3/38.]

Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "This is when lofty buildings are built, the visible (mounts) are ridden, and the famous garments are worn."

Wahb said: "There succeeded after them a successor who drink the coffees, play with the cubes, ride the passions, follow pleasures, abandon the Friday prayers [in the Isfahan copy: the congregations], and neglect the prayers." Ka'b said: "At the end of time there will appear people with whips in their hands like cows' tails, striking people," then he recited, "There succeeded after them a successor; they neglected the prayer and followed the passions."

So they will meet error (ghayy). Ibn Mas'ud said: "Al-Ghayy is a fire [in the Isfahan copy: a river] in Hell." Ibn Abbas said: "Al-Ghayy is a valley in Hell, and the valleys of Hell seek refuge from its heat. It is prepared for the fornicator who persists in it, the wine-drinker who is addicted to it, the eater of usury who does not desist from it, the people of disobedience to parents, the false witness, and a woman who introduced a child into her husband's household." Ata said: "Al-Ghayy is a valley in Hell that flows with pus and blood." Wahb said: "Al-Ghayy is a river in the Fire, deep in its bottom and foul in its taste." Ka'b said: "It is a valley in Hell, the deepest in its bottom and the most intense in its heat; in it is a well called al-Buhaym, whenever Hell subsides God opens that well and Hell is kindled by it." Al-Dahhak said: "Loss; and it was said: punishment; and it was said: pain; and it was said: disbelief."

Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds; those will enter the Garden and will not be wronged in the least. Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen, though they have not seen them. Indeed His promise is ever coming, meaning "ātiyan" (coming). Al-A'sha said:

"And I was walking with one disobedient toward her, and her goader."

That is, "'āṣiyan" (disobedient).

They will not hear therein, in the Garden, any vain talk (laghw), falsehood, obscenity, or superfluous speech. Muqatil said: "a false oath." Except "salaman" (peace), an exception from other than its kind, meaning they will hear therein only peace, that is, speech from which they are safe. The commentators said: this means their greeting one another, and the greeting of the angels to them. And for them their provision therein morning and evening, meaning in measure of the two ends of the day.

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far informed us, reading to him, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sakhtawayh told us, saying: Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-Darir told us, saying: Amdh ibn Siyaq told us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: In their time the Arabs considered one who had a lunch with a dinner to be a man of ease. So God revealed, "And for them their provision therein morning and evening," the measure between their lunch and dinner.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sakhtawayh told us, saying: Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Dawud ibn Rashid told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: I asked Zuhayr ibn Muhammad about God's words, "And for them their provision therein morning and evening," and he said: "There is no night in the Garden; they are always in light, and they know the measure of night only by the lowering of the veils, and the measure of day by the raising of the veils."

That is the Garden which We will cause to inherit from Our servants who were God-fearing. Ya'qub recited "nuwarrithu" with doubling, but the preferred reading is the lighter, because of His words, "Then We caused to inherit" [al-Fatir: 32]. "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord" [Maryam: 64], the verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ['Muhammad ibn' in the Isfahan copy] Abdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh ibn Ubadah told us, saying: Umar ibn Dharr told us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, what prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?" So God revealed, "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord."

Mujahid said: The messengers were delayed from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then Jibril came to him, and he said: "What detained you?" He said: "How could we come to you when you do not trim your nails, nor take your mustaches, nor use the siwak?" [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/137.] So God revealed, "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord," the verse.

Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil, Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: Jibril was held back from the Prophet (ﷺ) when his people asked him about the story of the People of the Cave, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, and he did not know how to answer them, hoping that Jibril would bring him the answer to what they asked, but he was delayed. Ikrimah said: forty days. Mujahid said: twelve nights. It was also said: fifteen. This was a severe hardship upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and abandoned him." When Jibril came down, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "You delayed me until my opinion grew bad and I longed for you." Jibril said to him: "I used to long for you more, but I am a servant under command: when I am sent I descend, and when I am held back I am held back." So God, exalted, revealed, "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord," and He revealed, "By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you" [al-Duha: 1-3].

It was also said: this is information about the people of the Garden, that they say upon entering it: "These gardens do not descend except by the command of God." "To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us, and what is between that." Muqatil said: to Him belongs what is before us of the affairs of the Hereafter, and what is behind us of the affairs of this world, and what is between that, meaning between the two blasts, and between them is forty years. It was also said: to Him belongs the beginning of our creation, and to Him belongs the end of our terms, and to Him belongs the duration of our lives.

It is said: "What is before us" is the reward and punishment and the matters of the Hereafter; "what is behind us" is what has passed of our deeds in this world; "what is between that" is what will happen from us until the Day of Resurrection. It is said: "to Him belongs what is before us" before He creates us, "and what is behind us" after He makes us die, "and what is between that" is what we are in of life. It is said: "to Him belongs what is before us" up to the earth when we want to descend to it, "and what is behind us," that is, the heaven when we descend from it, "and what is between that," meaning the heaven and the earth, intending that all of that belongs to God, glorified, so none of us is able to do anything except by His command.

"And your Lord was never forgetful" — that is, forgetful: when He wishes to send to you, He sends. "Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship" — that is, be patient in His worship. "Do you know anyone worthy of His name?" Ibn Abbas said: "a like." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "an equal." Al-Kalbi said: "Do you know anyone called God other than Him?"

"And man says: 'When I die, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?'" — meaning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, mockingly and denying resurrection.

God, glorified, said: "Does man not remember," that is, recall and reflect; the root is "yatadhakkar." Ibn Amir, Nafi', 'Asim and Ya'qub read "yadhkuru" with lightness, but the preferred reading is with doubling, because of His words, "Only those of understanding remember" [al-Ra'd: 19], and its like, and it is supported by Ubayy's reading "yatadhakkaru al-insan." Man, meaning Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, that "We created him before, and he was nothing." Then He swore by Himself, saying, "So by your Lord, We will surely gather them," that is, gather them for the Return, meaning the polytheists who deny resurrection, "and the devils with them," meaning their companions who misled them, each disbeliever being bound in a chain with a devil. "Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell," that is, within Hell, "on their knees." Ibn Abbas said: "groups upon groups." Muqatil said: "all together," and on this view it is the plural of "juthwah." Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: "kneeling on their knees," and on this interpretation it is the plural of "jathin." Al-Kumayt said:

"They left their nobles kneeling, while they were humbled beneath the nobles."

"Then We will surely draw out from every faction," that is, bring out from every community and religion, "whichever of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful." Ibn Abbas said: "that is, audacity." Mujahid said: "wickedness and lying." Muqatil said: "haughtiness." It was said: "extremism in disbelief," and it was said: "disbelief." Al-Kalbi said: "their leader is their chief in evil."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali told us, saying: Abu Usamah told us, from Sufyan, from Ali ibn al-Aqram, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: "We begin with the greatest, then the greatest." "Then indeed We are most knowing of those most deserving of entering it [the Fire]," that is, most worthy of entry into the Fire. It is said: "saliya yuslaa saliyyan," like "laqiya yalqa laqiyyan," and "salā yaṣlā ṣaliyyan," like "mada yamdi madiyyan."

And mention in the Book Idris; indeed he was a truthful man, a prophet. [Note: translating faithfully below.]

Actually, I must give the translation only, without notes. Here it is:

And mention in the Book Idris. He was the grandfather of Nuh's father, and he was named Idris for his great study of books (dars). His name was Akhnukh, and he was a tailor. He was the first to write with the pen, the first to sew garments and wear stitched clothing, and the first to speak on the science of the stars and calculation. Indeed he was a man of truth (siddiq), a prophet, and We raised him to a high station, meaning Paradise.

Al-Dahhak said: He was raised to the sixth heaven. It was also said: the fourth.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani and Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi informed us, both saying: Makki ibn Abdan al-Tamimi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning His words "and We raised him to a high station," he said: Anas ibn Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah told us that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was taken up to the heaven, said: "I came upon Idris in the heaven: the fourth." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 5/293.] ...

The cause of his being raised, according to what Ibn Abbas, Ka'b and others said, was that he walked one day on an errand, and the heat of the sun struck him, and he said: "O Lord, I walked one day, so how about one who carries it for five hundred years in a single day? O God, lighten its weight from him and bear its heat for him." When the angel woke in the morning, he found from the lightness and heat of the sun what was unknown. He said: "O Lord, You created me to carry the sun; what have You decreed for it?" He said: "As for My servant Idris, he asked Me to lighten its burden and heat for you, and I answered him." He said: "O Lord, bring me together with him and make a friendship between me and him." Permission was given to him, and he came to Idris, who was asking him questions. Among what he asked was: "I have been told that you are the most honored of the angels and the most influential with the Angel of Death. So intercede for me with him that he delay my term," so that he would increase in gratitude and worship. The angel said: "God does not delay a soul when its term comes." He said: "I know that, but it is more comforting to my soul." He said: "Yes, I will speak to him for you; whatever he could do for any of the sons of Adam, he will do for you." Then the angel of the sun carried him on his wing, raised him to the heaven, and placed him at the rising place of the sun. Then he came to the Angel of Death and said: "I have a need of you." He said: "I will do anything I am able to." He said: "A friend of mine from the sons of Adam seeks your intercession with you that you delay his term." He said: "That is not up to me, but if you wish, I will inform him of his term, when he will die, so that he may prepare himself." He said: "Yes." So he looked in his register and informed him of his name, and said: "You spoke to me about a man whom I do not see dying ever." He said: "How so?" He said: "I do not find him dying except at the rising of the sun." He said: "I came to you and left him there." He said: "Go, for I do not think you will find him except that he has died." By God, nothing remained of Idris's term, and the angel returned and found him dead.

Wahb said: Each day there was raised for Idris worship equal to what was raised for all the people of the earth in his time, and the angels marvelled at him, and the Angel of Death longed to meet him. He asked his Lord permission to visit him, and it was granted. He came to him in the form of a son of Adam. Idris was fasting, observing the fast of the whole year. When it was time for his breaking of the fast, he invited him to his food, but he refused to eat with him. This happened for three nights, and Idris disapproved of it. On the third night he said to him: "I want to know who you are." He said: "I am the Angel of Death; I asked my Lord to accompany you, and He permitted me." He said: "Then I have a need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Take my soul." God, mighty and majestic, revealed to him: "Take his soul," so he took his soul, and God returned it to him after an hour.

The Angel of Death said to him: "What is the benefit of your asking me to take the soul?" He said: "That I may taste the anguish and distress of death, so that I may be more prepared for it." Then Idris said to him: "I have another need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Raise me to the heaven so that I may look at it, and at the Garden and the Fire." God permitted him to raise him to the heavens. When he drew near the Fire, he said: "A need." He said: "What do you want?" He said: "Ask Malik to open its gate for me so I may return." He did so. Then he said: "Just as you showed me the Fire, show me the Garden." He took him to the Garden, asked for entry, and its gates were opened, and he entered him into the Garden. Then the Angel of Death said to him: "Come out, that you may return to your abode." But he clung to a tree and said: "I will not come out of it." So God sent an angel as judge between them, to consider their words. The angel said to him: "Why will you not come out?" He said: "Because God, exalted, said: 'Every soul shall taste death' [Al 'Imran: 85], and I have tasted it; and He said: 'There is none of you but will come to it' [Maryam: 71], and I have come to it; and He said: 'They will not be removed from it' [al-Hijr: 48], so I will not come out." God, glorified, revealed to the Angel of Death: "Enter the Garden, and by My command he will come out." He is alive there, and that is His words: "and We raised him to a high station."
