And with it, from Rawh, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first group passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts; then they pass, while the angels say: O God, grant safety, grant safety."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Idris told us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said to his brother: "O brother, has it reached you that you will arrive at the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will come out of it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laughter?" So he was never seen laughing until he died.

And with its chain, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Malik ibn Muʿawwal, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Maysarah, that he retired to his bed and said: "Would that my mother had not borne me!" His wife said: "O Abu Maysarah, God, glorified is He, has been good to you; He guided you to Islam." He said: "Indeed, but God has made clear to us that we will arrive at the Fire, and He has not made clear to us that we will depart from it." He also recited a verse on this meaning:

"The arrival at the Fire has come to us, pressing, / truly, certainly, though the departure has not yet come to us."

If it is said: Tell us, do the prophets enter the Fire? It is said to them: this term is not applied exclusively to them; rather we say that all creation will pass over it.

If they argue with His words: And when he arrived at the water of Madyan (Quran 28:23), it is said to them: Moses did not pass by that well; he only drew water for the two daughters of Shuʿayb and watered the flocks and then stayed, and this is the meaning of entry. The Arabs use the mention of water to refer to a people and their dwellings, so they say: "the water of the Banu so-and-so."

If it is said: How can one who, God has informed, will not hear its faint sound and will not enter it, enter it? It is said: God, glorified is He, has informed about the time of their being in Paradise that they will not hear its faint sound; so it is possible that they heard it before entering Paradise, since God, glorified is He, did not say "they will not have heard its faint sound," and it is possible that they will not hear its faint sound when they enter it, since God, Mighty and Majestic, is able to make it cool and peaceful for them.

Likewise the interpretation of His words "they will not enter the Fire" is: they will not abide in it, or they will not suffer or be harmed by it. This is indicated by what ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar told us, saying: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il told us, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Anas, concerning the words of God, glorified is He: "Indeed, whomever You admit to the Fire, You have truly disgraced him" (Quran 3:192): he said: "Indeed, whoever abides in the Fire, You have disgraced him."

The evidence that all creation enters the Fire, and then God saves the believers—some of them safe and unharmed, and some of them punished and recompensed—and then He admits them all into Paradise by His mercy, is what:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Abiwardi told us, saying: Abu Sa'id told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I hope that, God willing, no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyah will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of God, has not God said: And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is a decree decreed by your Lord (Quran 19:71)?" He said: "Did you not hear Him say: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)?"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us, saying: Jabghuyah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Musayyab informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Badr, from Abu Mas'ud, from al-ʿAbbas, from Ka'b, that he said concerning this verse, And there is none of you but will pass over it: "Hell will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a molten hide, and the feet of all creatures will stand upon it. A caller will call out: 'Take your companions and leave my companions!' and it will swallow them up, and it will know them better than a mother knows her child. The friends of God, glorified and exalted is He, will pass by with their garments unburned." Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: The people of Paradise will say: "Did not our Lord promise us that we would pass over the Fire?" It will be said: "Yes, but you passed by it while it was extinguished."

Khalid ibn Abi al-Duraik related from Ya'la ibn Munabbih that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection the Fire will say to the believer: 'Pass over, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame.'"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Harithi told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from ʿUthman al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: "Whoever among the Muslims is struck by fever has passed over it."

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi ʿArubah told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a barley grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a wheat grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of an atom."

Then We shall save those who were god-fearing: that is, those who feared shirk, and they are the believers. In the codex of ʿAbd Allah it is read "thumma nunajjī" with the tha' vowelled with a fatha, meaning "there" (hunāka). And We shall leave the wrongdoers therein: that is, the disbelievers, in the Fire, on their knees, all of them. It has also been said: "on their knees."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Sa'id ibn ʿAmir told us, from Hushaysh Abu Mahriz, who said: I heard Abu ʿImran al-Jawni say: "Suppose you are saved after your lot—how will you be saved?"

And when Our clear signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: (Quran 19:73). Those who disbelieve: that is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and those below him among the Quraysh. To those who believe: that is the poor companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who had austerity in them, roughness in their livelihood, and shabbiness in their clothes, whereas the polytheists would comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear their finest clothes. So they said to the believers: Which of the two groups is better in station (maqam), i.e., dwelling and abode, and better in assembly (nadiyy)? The people of Mecca read maqaman with a ḍamma, meaning "residence" (iqamah). And better in assembly: that is, a gathering; and similar to it is al-nādī, and from it comes Dar al-Nadwah, because the polytheists would sit there and consult on their affairs. God, Exalted, responded to them: And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in furnishing (athāth), i.e., possessions. Ibn ʿAbbas said: appearance. Muqatil said: garments. And better in show (ri'yan): i.e., in appearance. Ubayy read wazayyan with a zay, which means appearance.

Say: whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension (Quran 19:75). That is: let him leave him in his transgression and give him respite in his disbelief, until when they see what they are promised, whether the punishment (al-'adhab) in this world, or the Hour, meaning the Resurrection. Then they will know who is worse in place and weaker in army: they or the believers.

And God increases those who are guided in guidance (Quran 19:76): that is, faith and certainty, meaning the believers. It is said: "And God increases those who are guided"—with the abrogated (al-mansukh) guidance, with the abrogating (al-nasikh). And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in return (Quran 19:76): i.e., in outcome and in return. Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? (Quran 19:77)

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: I had a debt owed to al-As [in one copy of Isfahan: "ibn Wa'il"]. I came to him to demand it, and he said: "No, by God, not until you disbelieve in Muhammad." I said: "No, by God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are then resurrected." He said: "When I die and am resurrected, I will come to you, and then I will have wealth and children, and I will pay you." So God, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt was a smith who worked for al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, and al-As would delay his due from time to time until the season. Khabbab was insistent in his demand. He made some jewelry for him, and came to ask for his wage. Al-As said: "I do not have anything to pay you today." Khabbab said: "I will not leave you until you pay." Al-As said: "O Khabbab, what is wrong with you? You were not like this, though you were insistent and sociable." Khabbab said: "That is because I was on your religion, but today I am on Islam, separated from your religion, so no." He said: "Do you not claim that in Paradise there is gold, silver and silk?" Khabbab said: "Yes." He said: "Then delay me until I pay you in Paradise"—mockingly—"by God, if what you say is true, I will have a better share there than you." So God, glorified is He, revealed: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? That is al-As. And said: "I will surely be given wealth and children" (Quran 19:77). Ibn ʿAbbas said: Did he look into the Preserved Tablet? Mujahid said: He knows the unseen, so that he knows whether he will be in Paradise or not? Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? (Quran 19:78): that is, has he said "There is no god but God"? Qatadah said: that is, a righteous deed he had sent forward. Al-Kalbi said: He was promised that He would admit him to Paradise. No! (Quran 19:79): a rejection of him; that is, he has not done that. We will record what he says (Quran 19:79): We will preserve against him what he says, [in one copy of Isfahan, an addition: "and We will recompense him for it in the Hereafter, and We will extend for him an extension of punishment, meaning We will increase him in punishment above punishment... and We will inherit from him what he says"], meaning the wealth and children. And he will come to Us alone (Quran 19:80), in the Hereafter, with nothing with him.

And they have taken, besides God, gods (Quran 19:81), that is, the polytheists of Quraysh, idols, so that they may be for them a source of might (Quran 19:81). No! They will disbelieve in their worship (Quran 19:82) in the Hereafter, and will disown them, and they will be opposed to them (Quran 19:82): enemies. It is also said: helpers.

Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers (Quran 19:83)? That is, We have given them power over them, at the time He said to Iblis: "And incite whomever you can among them with your voice," and the verse.

They incite them with an incitement (Quran 19:83). Ibn ʿAbbas said: they stir them up, driving them from obedience to disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: they command them to sins, commanding. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they urge them on urging. Mujahid said: they stir them up stirring. Al-Akhfash said: they excite them. Al-Mu'arrikh said: they move them. Abu ʿUbayd said: they lead them astray and agitate them. Al-Qutaybi said: they drive them out to sins, and its root is motion and boiling, and from it comes the report of the Prophet (ﷺ): "And in his chest there is a murmur like the murmur of a boiling cauldron."

So do not hasten against them (Quran 19:84) with punishment; We are only counting for them a count (Quran 19:84). Al-Kalbi said: that is, the nights, days, months and years. It is also said: the breaths. It is said that al-Ma'mun was reciting Surat Maryam while the jurists were with him, and when he reached this verse he turned to Muhammad ibn al-Sammak, indicating that he should admonish him. He said: "When breaths are counted, and they have no supply, how quickly they will be exhausted."

The day We gather the god-fearing (muttaqin) (Quran 19:85): that is, the monotheists, to the Most Merciful as a delegation (wafdan): that is, in groups. It is the plural of wafid, like rakib and rakb, and sahib and sahb.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, saying: ...Wahb ibn Jarir told us, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah: The day We gather the god-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation (Quran 19:85): he said: "On camels." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "as riders, who are brought she-camels with saddles of gold and their reins of chrysolite, and they are mounted upon them."

And ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said:

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 19, verses 71–87 (Part 2 of 2)**

"They will not be gathered on their feet. Rather, they will be gathered on she-camels whose saddles are gold, and on noble mounts whose saddles are rubies. If they wish to move, they move; if they wish to fly, they fly." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/465, with variations.]]

Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid [[In a copy from Isfahan there is an addition: al-Wazzan.]] said: Akhbarana Ahmad ibn Shadhan, from Sa'ubah ibn Muhammad, who said: Haddathana Salih ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn ʿan Salih ibn Sadaqah, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When this verse was revealed, *"On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation"* [Qur'an 19:85], I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have seen the delegations of kings, and I have seen no delegation except riding." So what is the delegation of Allah?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'Ali, when the one who is dismissed from before Allah departs, the angels will meet the believers with white she-camels whose saddles and reins are gold. Upon each mount is a garment worth more than this world. Every believer will put on his garment, then they will mount their rides, and the she-camels will swoop with them until they reach Paradise, where the angels will greet them: *'Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it, abiding forever'* [Qur'an 39:73]." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/152.]]

Al-Rabi' said: *"On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation"* means they will come to their Lord, be honored, be given, be granted life, and be permitted to intercede. *"And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd to water"* [19:86], meaning the disbelievers. The commentators said: *"wirdan"* means thirsty, going on foot, their necks parched from thirst. *Al-warid* is a group coming to water; it is a noun in the form of a verbal noun.

*"They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful"* [19:87]. This means the declaration that there is no god but Allah. *Man* (who) is in the accusative position as an exception (*istithna'*).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It means that none will intercede except one who testified that there is no god but Allah, who disavowed power and strength, and who hopes only in Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Some of them said: Its meaning is "except for the one who has taken," and its parallel is *"And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves"* [21:28]. Muqatil said: *"except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful"* means one who held to monotheism.

Qatadah said: one who acted in obedience to Allah.

Abu Wa'il narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to his companions one day: "Is any of you unable to make for himself a covenant with Allah every morning and evening?"

They said: "How is that?" He said: "He says every morning and evening: *'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I make a covenant with You in this worldly life that I testify that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your messenger, and that if You leave me to myself, You bring me near to evil and distance me from good. I trust only in Your mercy, so make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill on the Day of Resurrection, for indeed You do not fail in the promise.'* When he says that, Allah seals it with a seal and places it beneath the Throne. On the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call: *'Where are those who have a covenant with the Most Merciful?'* and they will enter Paradise." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/62.]]

And there is none of you but will pass over it (Quran 19:71). It has been said: in the verse there is an implied meaning, namely: "By God, there is none of you [who will not come to it]," i.e., there is no one among you except that he will pass over it (wārid), meaning the Fire. People have differed concerning the meaning of wurūd (arrival/passing), in line with their differing views on the threat (wa'īd). As for the threat, they said: whoever enters it will not come out of it, and the Murji'ah said: no believer will enter it. They all agreed that wurūd means presence and passing. As for the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah), they said: it is permissible for God, glorified is He, to punish the disobedient among the believers with the Fire and then bring them out of it. They said: the meaning of wurūd is entry (dukhūl). They argued with the words of God, glorified is He, related as a report about Pharaoh: He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led (Quran 11:98). And He said concerning the idols and their worshippers: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (Quran 21:98). Had they been gods, they would not have arrived at it (Quran 21:99). So if wurūd in these verses did not mean entry, it would follow that the idols, their worshippers, Pharaoh and his people would enter Paradise, because whoever passes by the Fire must necessarily go to Paradise, since after this world there is no abode except Paradise or the Fire. What indicates that wurūd is entry is His words in the context of the verse: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing (Quran 19:72), and salvation can only be from that into which you have entered while being cast into it. God, glorified is He, said: And We saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers (Quran 21:88). The language also supports this: the Arabs say, "The letter of so-and-so arrived (wurida)," and "I arrived at such-and-such a city (waradtu baladan kadhā)," not meaning that they passed by it but that they entered it. Our evidence also comes from the Sunnah.

Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Faqih informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasr ibn Mansur al-Sa'igh, the righteous shaykh, told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, saying: Abu Salih Ghalib ibn Sulayman told us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad al-Barsani, from Abu Sumayya, who said: We differed about the wurūd here in Basra. Some people said: No believer will enter it; others said: They will all enter it. So I met Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah and asked him. He pointed with his two fingers to his ears and said: "May they be deaf if I did not hear the Prophet (ﷺ) say:

"The wurūd is entry. No righteous nor wicked person will remain but that he enters it; it will be cool and peaceful for the believer, just as it was for Ibrahim, so much so that the Fire, or Hell, will have a roar for those who approach it. Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)."

And Shuʿayb ibn Muhammad and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh ibn ʿUbadah told us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah told us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, that Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq saw Ibn ʿAbbas (saying): "The wurūd is entry," and Nafiʿ said: "The wurūd is not entry." Ibn ʿAbbas recited: You and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (Quran 21:98). "Did these enter or not?" Then he recited: He will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led (Quran 11:98). "Did these enter or not?" By God, you and I will indeed arrive there, and I hope that God will bring me out of it, but I do not think God will bring you out of it because of your denial.

And with its chain, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim whose three children die will enter the Fire, except for the fulfilment of the oath," and then he recited: And there is none of you but will pass over it.

And with its chain, from Rawh, who said: Shuʿbah told us, saying: Isma'il al-Suddi informed me, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Masʿud concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: They will pass through it and then depart from it according to their deeds.

And with it, from Rawh, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first group passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts; then they pass, while the angels say: O God, grant safety, grant safety."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Idris told us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said to his brother: "O brother, has it reached you that you will arrive at the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will come out of it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laughter?" So he was never seen laughing until he died.

And with its chain, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Malik ibn Muʿawwal, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Maysarah, that he retired to his bed and said: "Would that my mother had not borne me!" His wife said: "O Abu Maysarah, God, glorified is He, has been good to you; He guided you to Islam." He said: "Indeed, but God has made clear to us that we will arrive at the Fire, and He has not made clear to us that we will depart from it." He also recited a verse on this meaning:

"The arrival at the Fire has come to us, pressing, / truly, certainly, though the departure has not yet come to us."

If it is said: Tell us, do the prophets enter the Fire? It is said to them: this term is not applied exclusively to them; rather we say that all creation will pass over it.

If they argue with His words: And when he arrived at the water of Madyan (Quran 28:23), it is said to them: Moses did not pass by that well; he only drew water for the two daughters of Shuʿayb and watered the flocks and then stayed, and this is the meaning of entry. The Arabs use the mention of water to refer to a people and their dwellings, so they say: "the water of the Banu so-and-so."

If it is said: How can one who, God has informed, will not hear its faint sound and will not enter it, enter it? It is said: God, glorified is He, has informed about the time of their being in Paradise that they will not hear its faint sound; so it is possible that they heard it before entering Paradise, since God, glorified is He, did not say "they will not have heard its faint sound," and it is possible that they will not hear its faint sound when they enter it, since God, Mighty and Majestic, is able to make it cool and peaceful for them.

Likewise the interpretation of His words "they will not enter the Fire" is: they will not abide in it, or they will not suffer or be harmed by it. This is indicated by what ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar told us, saying: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il told us, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Anas, concerning the words of God, glorified is He: "Indeed, whomever You admit to the Fire, You have truly disgraced him" (Quran 3:192): he said: "Indeed, whoever abides in the Fire, You have disgraced him."

The evidence that all creation enters the Fire, and then God saves the believers—some of them safe and unharmed, and some of them punished and recompensed—and then He admits them all into Paradise by His mercy, is what:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Abiwardi told us, saying: Abu Sa'id told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I hope that, God willing, no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyah will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of God, has not God said: And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is a decree decreed by your Lord (Quran 19:71)?" He said: "Did you not hear Him say: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)?"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us, saying: Jabghuyah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Musayyab informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Badr, from Abu Mas'ud, from al-ʿAbbas, from Ka'b, that he said concerning this verse, And there is none of you but will pass over it: "Hell will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a molten hide, and the feet of all creatures will stand upon it. A caller will call out: 'Take your companions and leave my companions!' and it will swallow them up, and it will know them better than a mother knows her child. The friends of God, glorified and exalted is He, will pass by with their garments unburned." Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: The people of Paradise will say: "Did not our Lord promise us that we would pass over the Fire?" It will be said: "Yes, but you passed by it while it was extinguished."

Khalid ibn Abi al-Duraik related from Ya'la ibn Munabbih that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection the Fire will say to the believer: 'Pass over, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame.'"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Harithi told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from ʿUthman al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: "Whoever among the Muslims is struck by fever has passed over it."

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi ʿArubah told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a barley grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a wheat grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of an atom."

Then We shall save those who were god-fearing: that is, those who feared shirk, and they are the believers. In the codex of ʿAbd Allah it is read "thumma nunajjī" with the tha' vowelled with a fatha, meaning "there" (hunāka). And We shall leave the wrongdoers therein: that is, the disbelievers, in the Fire, on their knees, all of them. It has also been said: "on their knees."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Sa'id ibn ʿAmir told us, from Hushaysh Abu Mahriz, who said: I heard Abu ʿImran al-Jawni say: "Suppose you are saved after your lot—how will you be saved?"

And when Our clear signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: (Quran 19:73). Those who disbelieve: that is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and those below him among the Quraysh. To those who believe: that is the poor companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who had austerity in them, roughness in their livelihood, and shabbiness in their clothes, whereas the polytheists would comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear their finest clothes. So they said to the believers: Which of the two groups is better in station (maqam), i.e., dwelling and abode, and better in assembly (nadiyy)? The people of Mecca read maqaman with a ḍamma, meaning "residence" (iqamah). And better in assembly: that is, a gathering; and similar to it is al-nādī, and from it comes Dar al-Nadwah, because the polytheists would sit there and consult on their affairs. God, Exalted, responded to them: And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in furnishing (athāth), i.e., possessions. Ibn ʿAbbas said: appearance. Muqatil said: garments. And better in show (ri'yan): i.e., in appearance. Ubayy read wazayyan with a zay, which means appearance.

Say: whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension (Quran 19:75). That is: let him leave him in his transgression and give him respite in his disbelief, until when they see what they are promised, whether the punishment (al-'adhab) in this world, or the Hour, meaning the Resurrection. Then they will know who is worse in place and weaker in army: they or the believers.

And God increases those who are guided in guidance (Quran 19:76): that is, faith and certainty, meaning the believers. It is said: "And God increases those who are guided"—with the abrogated (al-mansukh) guidance, with the abrogating (al-nasikh). And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in return (Quran 19:76): i.e., in outcome and in return. Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? (Quran 19:77)

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: I had a debt owed to al-As [in one copy of Isfahan: "ibn Wa'il"]. I came to him to demand it, and he said: "No, by God, not until you disbelieve in Muhammad." I said: "No, by God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are then resurrected." He said: "When I die and am resurrected, I will come to you, and then I will have wealth and children, and I will pay you." So God, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt was a smith who worked for al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, and al-As would delay his due from time to time until the season. Khabbab was insistent in his demand. He made some jewelry for him, and came to ask for his wage. Al-As said: "I do not have anything to pay you today." Khabbab said: "I will not leave you until you pay." Al-As said: "O Khabbab, what is wrong with you? You were not like this, though you were insistent and sociable." Khabbab said: "That is because I was on your religion, but today I am on Islam, separated from your religion, so no." He said: "Do you not claim that in Paradise there is gold, silver and silk?" Khabbab said: "Yes." He said: "Then delay me until I pay you in Paradise"—mockingly—"by God, if what you say is true, I will have a better share there than you." So God, glorified is He, revealed: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? That is al-As. And said: "I will surely be given wealth and children" (Quran 19:77). Ibn ʿAbbas said: Did he look into the Preserved Tablet? Mujahid said: He knows the unseen, so that he knows whether he will be in Paradise or not? Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? (Quran 19:78): that is, has he said "There is no god but God"? Qatadah said: that is, a righteous deed he had sent forward. Al-Kalbi said: He was promised that He would admit him to Paradise. No! (Quran 19:79): a rejection of him; that is, he has not done that. We will record what he says (Quran 19:79): We will preserve against him what he says, [in one copy of Isfahan, an addition: "and We will recompense him for it in the Hereafter, and We will extend for him an extension of punishment, meaning We will increase him in punishment above punishment... and We will inherit from him what he says"], meaning the wealth and children. And he will come to Us alone (Quran 19:80), in the Hereafter, with nothing with him.

And they have taken, besides God, gods (Quran 19:81), that is, the polytheists of Quraysh, idols, so that they may be for them a source of might (Quran 19:81). No! They will disbelieve in their worship (Quran 19:82) in the Hereafter, and will disown them, and they will be opposed to them (Quran 19:82): enemies. It is also said: helpers.

Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers (Quran 19:83)? That is, We have given them power over them, at the time He said to Iblis: "And incite whomever you can among them with your voice," and the verse.

They incite them with an incitement (Quran 19:83). Ibn ʿAbbas said: they stir them up, driving them from obedience to disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: they command them to sins, commanding. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they urge them on urging. Mujahid said: they stir them up stirring. Al-Akhfash said: they excite them. Al-Mu'arrikh said: they move them. Abu ʿUbayd said: they lead them astray and agitate them. Al-Qutaybi said: they drive them out to sins, and its root is motion and boiling, and from it comes the report of the Prophet (ﷺ): "And in his chest there is a murmur like the murmur of a boiling cauldron."

So do not hasten against them (Quran 19:84) with punishment; We are only counting for them a count (Quran 19:84). Al-Kalbi said: that is, the nights, days, months and years. It is also said: the breaths. It is said that al-Ma'mun was reciting Surat Maryam while the jurists were with him, and when he reached this verse he turned to Muhammad ibn al-Sammak, indicating that he should admonish him. He said: "When breaths are counted, and they have no supply, how quickly they will be exhausted."

The day We gather the god-fearing (muttaqin) (Quran 19:85): that is, the monotheists, to the Most Merciful as a delegation (wafdan): that is, in groups. It is the plural of wafid, like rakib and rakb, and sahib and sahb.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, saying: ...Wahb ibn Jarir told us, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah: The day We gather the god-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation (Quran 19:85): he said: "On camels." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "as riders, who are brought she-camels with saddles of gold and their reins of chrysolite, and they are mounted upon them."

And ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said:

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 19, verses 71–87 (Part 2 of 2)**

"They will not be gathered on their feet. Rather, they will be gathered on she-camels whose saddles are gold, and on noble mounts whose saddles are rubies. If they wish to move, they move; if they wish to fly, they fly." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/465, with variations.]]

Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid [[In a copy from Isfahan there is an addition: al-Wazzan.]] said: Akhbarana Ahmad ibn Shadhan, from Sa'ubah ibn Muhammad, who said: Haddathana Salih ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn ʿan Salih ibn Sadaqah, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When this verse was revealed, *"On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation"* [Qur'an 19:85], I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have seen the delegations of kings, and I have seen no delegation except riding." So what is the delegation of Allah?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'Ali, when the one who is dismissed from before Allah departs, the angels will meet the believers with white she-camels whose saddles and reins are gold. Upon each mount is a garment worth more than this world. Every believer will put on his garment, then they will mount their rides, and the she-camels will swoop with them until they reach Paradise, where the angels will greet them: *'Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it, abiding forever'* [Qur'an 39:73]." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/152.]]

Al-Rabi' said: *"On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation"* means they will come to their Lord, be honored, be given, be granted life, and be permitted to intercede. *"And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd to water"* [19:86], meaning the disbelievers. The commentators said: *"wirdan"* means thirsty, going on foot, their necks parched from thirst. *Al-warid* is a group coming to water; it is a noun in the form of a verbal noun.

*"They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful"* [19:87]. This means the declaration that there is no god but Allah. *Man* (who) is in the accusative position as an exception (*istithna'*).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It means that none will intercede except one who testified that there is no god but Allah, who disavowed power and strength, and who hopes only in Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Some of them said: Its meaning is "except for the one who has taken," and its parallel is *"And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves"* [21:28]. Muqatil said: *"except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful"* means one who held to monotheism.

Qatadah said: one who acted in obedience to Allah.

Abu Wa'il narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to his companions one day: "Is any of you unable to make for himself a covenant with Allah every morning and evening?"

They said: "How is that?" He said: "He says every morning and evening: *'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I make a covenant with You in this worldly life that I testify that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your messenger, and that if You leave me to myself, You bring me near to evil and distance me from good. I trust only in Your mercy, so make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill on the Day of Resurrection, for indeed You do not fail in the promise.'* When he says that, Allah seals it with a seal and places it beneath the Throne. On the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call: *'Where are those who have a covenant with the Most Merciful?'* and they will enter Paradise." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/62.]]

And there is none of you but will pass over it (Quran 19:71). It has been said: in the verse there is an implied meaning, namely: "By God, there is none of you [who will not come to it]," i.e., there is no one among you except that he will pass over it (wārid), meaning the Fire. People have differed concerning the meaning of wurūd (arrival/passing), in line with their differing views on the threat (wa'īd). As for the threat, they said: whoever enters it will not come out of it, and the Murji'ah said: no believer will enter it. They all agreed that wurūd means presence and passing. As for the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah), they said: it is permissible for God, glorified is He, to punish the disobedient among the believers with the Fire and then bring them out of it. They said: the meaning of wurūd is entry (dukhūl). They argued with the words of God, glorified is He, related as a report about Pharaoh: He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led (Quran 11:98). And He said concerning the idols and their worshippers: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (Quran 21:98). Had they been gods, they would not have arrived at it (Quran 21:99). So if wurūd in these verses did not mean entry, it would follow that the idols, their worshippers, Pharaoh and his people would enter Paradise, because whoever passes by the Fire must necessarily go to Paradise, since after this world there is no abode except Paradise or the Fire. What indicates that wurūd is entry is His words in the context of the verse: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing (Quran 19:72), and salvation can only be from that into which you have entered while being cast into it. God, glorified is He, said: And We saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers (Quran 21:88). The language also supports this: the Arabs say, "The letter of so-and-so arrived (wurida)," and "I arrived at such-and-such a city (waradtu baladan kadhā)," not meaning that they passed by it but that they entered it. Our evidence also comes from the Sunnah.

Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Faqih informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasr ibn Mansur al-Sa'igh, the righteous shaykh, told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, saying: Abu Salih Ghalib ibn Sulayman told us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad al-Barsani, from Abu Sumayya, who said: We differed about the wurūd here in Basra. Some people said: No believer will enter it; others said: They will all enter it. So I met Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah and asked him. He pointed with his two fingers to his ears and said: "May they be deaf if I did not hear the Prophet (ﷺ) say:

"The wurūd is entry. No righteous nor wicked person will remain but that he enters it; it will be cool and peaceful for the believer, just as it was for Ibrahim, so much so that the Fire, or Hell, will have a roar for those who approach it. Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)."

And Shuʿayb ibn Muhammad and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh ibn ʿUbadah told us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah told us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, that Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq saw Ibn ʿAbbas (saying): "The wurūd is entry," and Nafiʿ said: "The wurūd is not entry." Ibn ʿAbbas recited: You and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (Quran 21:98). "Did these enter or not?" Then he recited: He will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led (Quran 11:98). "Did these enter or not?" By God, you and I will indeed arrive there, and I hope that God will bring me out of it, but I do not think God will bring you out of it because of your denial.

And with its chain, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim whose three children die will enter the Fire, except for the fulfilment of the oath," and then he recited: And there is none of you but will pass over it.

And with its chain, from Rawh, who said: Shuʿbah told us, saying: Isma'il al-Suddi informed me, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Masʿud concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: They will pass through it and then depart from it according to their deeds.

And with it, from Rawh, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first group passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts; then they pass, while the angels say: O God, grant safety, grant safety."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Idris told us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said to his brother: "O brother, has it reached you that you will arrive at the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will come out of it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laughter?" So he was never seen laughing until he died.

And with its chain, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Malik ibn Muʿawwal, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Maysarah, that he retired to his bed and said: "Would that my mother had not borne me!" His wife said: "O Abu Maysarah, God, glorified is He, has been good to you; He guided you to Islam." He said: "Indeed, but God has made clear to us that we will arrive at the Fire, and He has not made clear to us that we will depart from it." He also recited a verse on this meaning:

"The arrival at the Fire has come to us, pressing, / truly, certainly, though the departure has not yet come to us."

If it is said: Tell us, do the prophets enter the Fire? It is said to them: this term is not applied exclusively to them; rather we say that all creation will pass over it.

If they argue with His words: And when he arrived at the water of Madyan (Quran 28:23), it is said to them: Moses did not pass by that well; he only drew water for the two daughters of Shuʿayb and watered the flocks and then stayed, and this is the meaning of entry. The Arabs use the mention of water to refer to a people and their dwellings, so they say: "the water of the Banu so-and-so."

If it is said: How can one who, God has informed, will not hear its faint sound and will not enter it, enter it? It is said: God, glorified is He, has informed about the time of their being in Paradise that they will not hear its faint sound; so it is possible that they heard it before entering Paradise, since God, glorified is He, did not say "they will not have heard its faint sound," and it is possible that they will not hear its faint sound when they enter it, since God, Mighty and Majestic, is able to make it cool and peaceful for them.

Likewise the interpretation of His words "they will not enter the Fire" is: they will not abide in it, or they will not suffer or be harmed by it. This is indicated by what ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar told us, saying: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il told us, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Anas, concerning the words of God, glorified is He: "Indeed, whomever You admit to the Fire, You have truly disgraced him" (Quran 3:192): he said: "Indeed, whoever abides in the Fire, You have disgraced him."

The evidence that all creation enters the Fire, and then God saves the believers—some of them safe and unharmed, and some of them punished and recompensed—and then He admits them all into Paradise by His mercy, is what:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Abiwardi told us, saying: Abu Sa'id told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I hope that, God willing, no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyah will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of God, has not God said: And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is a decree decreed by your Lord (Quran 19:71)?" He said: "Did you not hear Him say: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)?"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us, saying: Jabghuyah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Musayyab informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Badr, from Abu Mas'ud, from al-ʿAbbas, from Ka'b, that he said concerning this verse, And there is none of you but will pass over it: "Hell will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a molten hide, and the feet of all creatures will stand upon it. A caller will call out: 'Take your companions and leave my companions!' and it will swallow them up, and it will know them better than a mother knows her child. The friends of God, glorified and exalted is He, will pass by with their garments unburned." Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: The people of Paradise will say: "Did not our Lord promise us that we would pass over the Fire?" It will be said: "Yes, but you passed by it while it was extinguished."

Khalid ibn Abi al-Duraik related from Ya'la ibn Munabbih that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection the Fire will say to the believer: 'Pass over, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame.'"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Harithi told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from ʿUthman al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: "Whoever among the Muslims is struck by fever has passed over it."

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi ʿArubah told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a barley grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a wheat grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of an atom."

Then We shall save those who were god-fearing: that is, those who feared shirk, and they are the believers. In the codex of ʿAbd Allah it is read "thumma nunajjī" with the tha' vowelled with a fatha, meaning "there" (hunāka). And We shall leave the wrongdoers therein: that is, the disbelievers, in the Fire, on their knees, all of them. It has also been said: "on their knees."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Sa'id ibn ʿAmir told us, from Hushaysh Abu Mahriz, who said: I heard Abu ʿImran al-Jawni say: "Suppose you are saved after your lot—how will you be saved?"

And when Our clear signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: (Quran 19:73). Those who disbelieve: that is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and those below him among the Quraysh. To those who believe: that is the poor companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who had austerity in them, roughness in their livelihood, and shabbiness in their clothes, whereas the polytheists would comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear their finest clothes. So they said to the believers: Which of the two groups is better in station (maqam), i.e., dwelling and abode, and better in assembly (nadiyy)? The people of Mecca read maqaman with a ḍamma, meaning "residence" (iqamah). And better in assembly: that is, a gathering; and similar to it is al-nādī, and from it comes Dar al-Nadwah, because the polytheists would sit there and consult on their affairs. God, Exalted, responded to them: And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in furnishing (athāth), i.e., possessions. Ibn ʿAbbas said: appearance. Muqatil said: garments. And better in show (ri'yan): i.e., in appearance. Ubayy read wazayyan with a zay, which means appearance.

Say: whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension (Quran 19:75). That is: let him leave him in his transgression and give him respite in his disbelief, until when they see what they are promised, whether the punishment (al-'adhab) in this world, or the Hour, meaning the Resurrection. Then they will know who is worse in place and weaker in army: they or the believers.

And God increases those who are guided in guidance (Quran 19:76): that is, faith and certainty, meaning the believers. It is said: "And God increases those who are guided"—with the abrogated (al-mansukh) guidance, with the abrogating (al-nasikh). And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in return (Quran 19:76): i.e., in outcome and in return. Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? (Quran 19:77)

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: I had a debt owed to al-As [in one copy of Isfahan: "ibn Wa'il"]. I came to him to demand it, and he said: "No, by God, not until you disbelieve in Muhammad." I said: "No, by God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are then resurrected." He said: "When I die and am resurrected, I will come to you, and then I will have wealth and children, and I will pay you." So God, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt was a smith who worked for al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, and al-As would delay his due from time to time until the season. Khabbab was insistent in his demand. He made some jewelry for him, and came to ask for his wage. Al-As said: "I do not have anything to pay you today." Khabbab said: "I will not leave you until you pay." Al-As said: "O Khabbab, what is wrong with you? You were not like this, though you were insistent and sociable." Khabbab said: "That is because I was on your religion, but today I am on Islam, separated from your religion, so no." He said: "Do you not claim that in Paradise there is gold, silver and silk?" Khabbab said: "Yes." He said: "Then delay me until I pay you in Paradise"—mockingly—"by God, if what you say is true, I will have a better share there than you." So God, glorified is He, revealed: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? That is al-As. And said: "I will surely be given wealth and children" (Quran 19:77). Ibn ʿAbbas said: Did he look into the Preserved Tablet? Mujahid said: He knows the unseen, so that he knows whether he will be in Paradise or not? Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? (Quran 19:78): that is, has he said "There is no god but God"? Qatadah said: that is, a righteous deed he had sent forward. Al-Kalbi said: He was promised that He would admit him to Paradise. No! (Quran 19:79): a rejection of him; that is, he has not done that. We will record what he says (Quran 19:79): We will preserve against him what he says, [in one copy of Isfahan, an addition: "and We will recompense him for it in the Hereafter, and We will extend for him an extension of punishment, meaning We will increase him in punishment above punishment... and We will inherit from him what he says"], meaning the wealth and children. And he will come to Us alone (Quran 19:80), in the Hereafter, with nothing with him.

And they have taken, besides God, gods (Quran 19:81), that is, the polytheists of Quraysh, idols, so that they may be for them a source of might (Quran 19:81). No! They will disbelieve in their worship (Quran 19:82) in the Hereafter, and will disown them, and they will be opposed to them (Quran 19:82): enemies. It is also said: helpers.

Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers (Quran 19:83)? That is, We have given them power over them, at the time He said to Iblis: "And incite whomever you can among them with your voice," and the verse.

They incite them with an incitement (Quran 19:83). Ibn ʿAbbas said: they stir them up, driving them from obedience to disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: they command them to sins, commanding. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they urge them on urging. Mujahid said: they stir them up stirring. Al-Akhfash said: they excite them. Al-Mu'arrikh said: they move them. Abu ʿUbayd said: they lead them astray and agitate them. Al-Qutaybi said: they drive them out to sins, and its root is motion and boiling, and from it comes the report of the Prophet (ﷺ): "And in his chest there is a murmur like the murmur of a boiling cauldron."

So do not hasten against them (Quran 19:84) with punishment; We are only counting for them a count (Quran 19:84). Al-Kalbi said: that is, the nights, days, months and years. It is also said: the breaths. It is said that al-Ma'mun was reciting Surat Maryam while the jurists were with him, and when he reached this verse he turned to Muhammad ibn al-Sammak, indicating that he should admonish him. He said: "When breaths are counted, and they have no supply, how quickly they will be exhausted."

The day We gather the god-fearing (muttaqin) (Quran 19:85): that is, the monotheists, to the Most Merciful as a delegation (wafdan): that is, in groups. It is the plural of wafid, like rakib and rakb, and sahib and sahb.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, saying: ...Wahb ibn Jarir told us, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah: The day We gather the god-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation (Quran 19:85): he said: "On camels." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "as riders, who are brought she-camels with saddles of gold and their reins of chrysolite, and they are mounted upon them."

And ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said:

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 19, verses 71–87 (Part 2 of 2)**

"They will not be gathered on their feet. Rather, they will be gathered on she-camels whose saddles are gold, and on noble mounts whose saddles are rubies. If they wish to move, they move; if they wish to fly, they fly." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/465, with variations.]]

Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid [[In a copy from Isfahan there is an addition: al-Wazzan.]] said: Akhbarana Ahmad ibn Shadhan, from Sa'ubah ibn Muhammad, who said: Haddathana Salih ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn ʿan Salih ibn Sadaqah, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When this verse was revealed, *"On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation"* [Qur'an 19:85], I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have seen the delegations of kings, and I have seen no delegation except riding." So what is the delegation of Allah?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O 'Ali, when the one who is dismissed from before Allah departs, the angels will meet the believers with white she-camels whose saddles and reins are gold. Upon each mount is a garment worth more than this world. Every believer will put on his garment, then they will mount their rides, and the she-camels will swoop with them until they reach Paradise, where the angels will greet them: *'Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it, abiding forever'* [Qur'an 39:73]." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/152.]]

Al-Rabi' said: *"On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation"* means they will come to their Lord, be honored, be given, be granted life, and be permitted to intercede. *"And We will drive the criminals to Hell as a herd to water"* [19:86], meaning the disbelievers. The commentators said: *"wirdan"* means thirsty, going on foot, their necks parched from thirst. *Al-warid* is a group coming to water; it is a noun in the form of a verbal noun.

*"They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful"* [19:87]. This means the declaration that there is no god but Allah. *Man* (who) is in the accusative position as an exception (*istithna'*).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It means that none will intercede except one who testified that there is no god but Allah, who disavowed power and strength, and who hopes only in Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Some of them said: Its meaning is "except for the one who has taken," and its parallel is *"And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves"* [21:28]. Muqatil said: *"except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful"* means one who held to monotheism.

Qatadah said: one who acted in obedience to Allah.

Abu Wa'il narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to his companions one day: "Is any of you unable to make for himself a covenant with Allah every morning and evening?"

They said: "How is that?" He said: "He says every morning and evening: *'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I make a covenant with You in this worldly life that I testify that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your messenger, and that if You leave me to myself, You bring me near to evil and distance me from good. I trust only in Your mercy, so make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill on the Day of Resurrection, for indeed You do not fail in the promise.'* When he says that, Allah seals it with a seal and places it beneath the Throne. On the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call: *'Where are those who have a covenant with the Most Merciful?'* and they will enter Paradise." [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/62.]]

And there is none of you but will pass over it (Quran 19:71). It has been said: in the verse there is an implied meaning, namely: "By God, there is none of you [who will not come to it]," i.e., there is no one among you except that he will pass over it (wārid), meaning the Fire. People have differed concerning the meaning of wurūd (arrival/passing), in line with their differing views on the threat (wa'īd). As for the threat, they said: whoever enters it will not come out of it, and the Murji'ah said: no believer will enter it. They all agreed that wurūd means presence and passing. As for the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah), they said: it is permissible for God, glorified is He, to punish the disobedient among the believers with the Fire and then bring them out of it. They said: the meaning of wurūd is entry (dukhūl). They argued with the words of God, glorified is He, related as a report about Pharaoh: He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led (Quran 11:98). And He said concerning the idols and their worshippers: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (Quran 21:98). Had they been gods, they would not have arrived at it (Quran 21:99). So if wurūd in these verses did not mean entry, it would follow that the idols, their worshippers, Pharaoh and his people would enter Paradise, because whoever passes by the Fire must necessarily go to Paradise, since after this world there is no abode except Paradise or the Fire. What indicates that wurūd is entry is His words in the context of the verse: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing (Quran 19:72), and salvation can only be from that into which you have entered while being cast into it. God, glorified is He, said: And We saved him from the distress, and thus We save the believers (Quran 21:88). The language also supports this: the Arabs say, "The letter of so-and-so arrived (wurida)," and "I arrived at such-and-such a city (waradtu baladan kadhā)," not meaning that they passed by it but that they entered it. Our evidence also comes from the Sunnah.

Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Faqih informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasr ibn Mansur al-Sa'igh, the righteous shaykh, told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, saying: Abu Salih Ghalib ibn Sulayman told us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad al-Barsani, from Abu Sumayya, who said: We differed about the wurūd here in Basra. Some people said: No believer will enter it; others said: They will all enter it. So I met Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah and asked him. He pointed with his two fingers to his ears and said: "May they be deaf if I did not hear the Prophet (ﷺ) say:

"The wurūd is entry. No righteous nor wicked person will remain but that he enters it; it will be cool and peaceful for the believer, just as it was for Ibrahim, so much so that the Fire, or Hell, will have a roar for those who approach it. Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)."

And Shuʿayb ibn Muhammad and ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, both saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar told us, saying: Rawh ibn ʿUbadah told us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah told us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, that Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq saw Ibn ʿAbbas (saying): "The wurūd is entry," and Nafiʿ said: "The wurūd is not entry." Ibn ʿAbbas recited: You and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will arrive at it (Quran 21:98). "Did these enter or not?" Then he recited: He will lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led (Quran 11:98). "Did these enter or not?" By God, you and I will indeed arrive there, and I hope that God will bring me out of it, but I do not think God will bring you out of it because of your denial.

And with its chain, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim whose three children die will enter the Fire, except for the fulfilment of the oath," and then he recited: And there is none of you but will pass over it.

And with its chain, from Rawh, who said: Shuʿbah told us, saying: Isma'il al-Suddi informed me, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Masʿud concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: They will pass through it and then depart from it according to their deeds.

And with it, from Rawh, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "The Sirat over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first group passes like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts; then they pass, while the angels say: O God, grant safety, grant safety."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Harawi informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Idris told us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: A man said to his brother: "O brother, has it reached you that you will arrive at the Fire?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Has it reached you that you will come out of it?" He said: "No." He said: "Then why laughter?" So he was never seen laughing until he died.

And with its chain, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Malik ibn Muʿawwal, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Maysarah, that he retired to his bed and said: "Would that my mother had not borne me!" His wife said: "O Abu Maysarah, God, glorified is He, has been good to you; He guided you to Islam." He said: "Indeed, but God has made clear to us that we will arrive at the Fire, and He has not made clear to us that we will depart from it." He also recited a verse on this meaning:

"The arrival at the Fire has come to us, pressing, / truly, certainly, though the departure has not yet come to us."

If it is said: Tell us, do the prophets enter the Fire? It is said to them: this term is not applied exclusively to them; rather we say that all creation will pass over it.

If they argue with His words: And when he arrived at the water of Madyan (Quran 28:23), it is said to them: Moses did not pass by that well; he only drew water for the two daughters of Shuʿayb and watered the flocks and then stayed, and this is the meaning of entry. The Arabs use the mention of water to refer to a people and their dwellings, so they say: "the water of the Banu so-and-so."

If it is said: How can one who, God has informed, will not hear its faint sound and will not enter it, enter it? It is said: God, glorified is He, has informed about the time of their being in Paradise that they will not hear its faint sound; so it is possible that they heard it before entering Paradise, since God, glorified is He, did not say "they will not have heard its faint sound," and it is possible that they will not hear its faint sound when they enter it, since God, Mighty and Majestic, is able to make it cool and peaceful for them.

Likewise the interpretation of His words "they will not enter the Fire" is: they will not abide in it, or they will not suffer or be harmed by it. This is indicated by what ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar told us, saying: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il told us, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Anas, concerning the words of God, glorified is He: "Indeed, whomever You admit to the Fire, You have truly disgraced him" (Quran 3:192): he said: "Indeed, whoever abides in the Fire, You have disgraced him."

The evidence that all creation enters the Fire, and then God saves the believers—some of them safe and unharmed, and some of them punished and recompensed—and then He admits them all into Paradise by His mercy, is what:

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Abiwardi told us, saying: Abu Sa'id told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I hope that, God willing, no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyah will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of God, has not God said: And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is a decree decreed by your Lord (Quran 19:71)?" He said: "Did you not hear Him say: Then We shall save those who were god-fearing, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees (Quran 19:72)?"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us, saying: Jabghuyah ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Musayyab informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Badr, from Abu Mas'ud, from al-ʿAbbas, from Ka'b, that he said concerning this verse, And there is none of you but will pass over it: "Hell will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as if it were a molten hide, and the feet of all creatures will stand upon it. A caller will call out: 'Take your companions and leave my companions!' and it will swallow them up, and it will know them better than a mother knows her child. The friends of God, glorified and exalted is He, will pass by with their garments unburned." Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: The people of Paradise will say: "Did not our Lord promise us that we would pass over the Fire?" It will be said: "Yes, but you passed by it while it was extinguished."

Khalid ibn Abi al-Duraik related from Ya'la ibn Munabbih that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection the Fire will say to the believer: 'Pass over, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame.'"

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Harithi told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, from Yahya ibn Yaman, from ʿUthman al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning His words: And there is none of you but will pass over it, he said: "Whoever among the Muslims is struck by fever has passed over it."

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi ʿArubah told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a barley grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of a wheat grain; then there will come out of the Fire whoever said: 'There is no god but God' and had in his heart good the weight of an atom."

Then We shall save those who were god-fearing: that is, those who feared shirk, and they are the believers. In the codex of ʿAbd Allah it is read "thumma nunajjī" with the tha' vowelled with a fatha, meaning "there" (hunāka). And We shall leave the wrongdoers therein: that is, the disbelievers, in the Fire, on their knees, all of them. It has also been said: "on their knees."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman told us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd told us, saying: Sa'id ibn ʿAmir told us, from Hushaysh Abu Mahriz, who said: I heard Abu ʿImran al-Jawni say: "Suppose you are saved after your lot—how will you be saved?"

And when Our clear signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: (Quran 19:73). Those who disbelieve: that is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and those below him among the Quraysh. To those who believe: that is the poor companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who had austerity in them, roughness in their livelihood, and shabbiness in their clothes, whereas the polytheists would comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear their finest clothes. So they said to the believers: Which of the two groups is better in station (maqam), i.e., dwelling and abode, and better in assembly (nadiyy)? The people of Mecca read maqaman with a ḍamma, meaning "residence" (iqamah). And better in assembly: that is, a gathering; and similar to it is al-nādī, and from it comes Dar al-Nadwah, because the polytheists would sit there and consult on their affairs. God, Exalted, responded to them: And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in furnishing (athāth), i.e., possessions. Ibn ʿAbbas said: appearance. Muqatil said: garments. And better in show (ri'yan): i.e., in appearance. Ubayy read wazayyan with a zay, which means appearance.

Say: whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension (Quran 19:75). That is: let him leave him in his transgression and give him respite in his disbelief, until when they see what they are promised, whether the punishment (al-'adhab) in this world, or the Hour, meaning the Resurrection. Then they will know who is worse in place and weaker in army: they or the believers.

And God increases those who are guided in guidance (Quran 19:76): that is, faith and certainty, meaning the believers. It is said: "And God increases those who are guided"—with the abrogated (al-mansukh) guidance, with the abrogating (al-nasikh). And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in return (Quran 19:76): i.e., in outcome and in return. Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? (Quran 19:77)

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Warrazan informed us, saying: Makki ibn ʿAbdan informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, saying: al-A'mash told us, from Muslim, from Masruq, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: I had a debt owed to al-As [in one copy of Isfahan: "ibn Wa'il"]. I came to him to demand it, and he said: "No, by God, not until you disbelieve in Muhammad." I said: "No, by God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are then resurrected." He said: "When I die and am resurrected, I will come to you, and then I will have wealth and children, and I will pay you." So God, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt was a smith who worked for al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, and al-As would delay his due from time to time until the season. Khabbab was insistent in his demand. He made some jewelry for him, and came to ask for his wage. Al-As said: "I do not have anything to pay you today." Khabbab said: "I will not leave you until you pay." Al-As said: "O Khabbab, what is wrong with you? You were not like this, though you were insistent and sociable." Khabbab said: "That is because I was on your religion, but today I am on Islam, separated from your religion, so no." He said: "Do you not claim that in Paradise there is gold, silver and silk?" Khabbab said: "Yes." He said: "Then delay me until I pay you in Paradise"—mockingly—"by God, if what you say is true, I will have a better share there than you." So God, glorified is He, revealed: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs? That is al-As. And said: "I will surely be given wealth and children" (Quran 19:77). Ibn ʿAbbas said: Did he look into the Preserved Tablet? Mujahid said: He knows the unseen, so that he knows whether he will be in Paradise or not? Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? (Quran 19:78): that is, has he said "There is no god but God"? Qatadah said: that is, a righteous deed he had sent forward. Al-Kalbi said: He was promised that He would admit him to Paradise. No! (Quran 19:79): a rejection of him; that is, he has not done that. We will record what he says (Quran 19:79): We will preserve against him what he says, [in one copy of Isfahan, an addition: "and We will recompense him for it in the Hereafter, and We will extend for him an extension of punishment, meaning We will increase him in punishment above punishment... and We will inherit from him what he says"], meaning the wealth and children. And he will come to Us alone (Quran 19:80), in the Hereafter, with nothing with him.

And they have taken, besides God, gods (Quran 19:81), that is, the polytheists of Quraysh, idols, so that they may be for them a source of might (Quran 19:81). No! They will disbelieve in their worship (Quran 19:82) in the Hereafter, and will disown them, and they will be opposed to them (Quran 19:82): enemies. It is also said: helpers.

Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers (Quran 19:83)? That is, We have given them power over them, at the time He said to Iblis: "And incite whomever you can among them with your voice," and the verse.

They incite them with an incitement (Quran 19:83). Ibn ʿAbbas said: they stir them up, driving them from obedience to disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: they command them to sins, commanding. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they urge them on urging. Mujahid said: they stir them up stirring. Al-Akhfash said: they excite them. Al-Mu'arrikh said: they move them. Abu ʿUbayd said: they lead them astray and agitate them. Al-Qutaybi said: they drive them out to sins, and its root is motion and boiling, and from it comes the report of the Prophet (ﷺ): "And in his chest there is a murmur like the murmur of a boiling cauldron."

So do not hasten against them (Quran 19:84) with punishment; We are only counting for them a count (Quran 19:84). Al-Kalbi said: that is, the nights, days, months and years. It is also said: the breaths.
